# Amazon Relay scorecard: how the performance score works and how to dispute it

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-04.

Short answer: The Amazon Relay scorecard gives each carrier a performance score from 0% to 100%, shown as a letter grade from F to A+. It covers the last six weeks of hauls and four metrics: on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free. The overall score equals the lowest of the four, and higher grades open auctions, contracts and early spot loads.

## What is the Amazon Relay scorecard?

The Amazon Relay scorecard is the performance score Amazon gives every Relay carrier. It runs from 0% to 100% and shows as a letter grade from F to A+. It reflects your last six weeks of hauls, and your grade decides which freight you can reach on Relay, from auctions and contracts to early access on new spot loads.

You find it in your Relay account. Amazon explains the system on its [performance score page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score) and in its guide to [performance grades](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities).

Two numbers to know:

- **Six weeks.** The score looks at your recent hauls, not your whole history.
- **Ten loads.** You become eligible for a grade after completing ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks.

If you are new and still setting up, start with [what Amazon Relay is](https://nudoiq.com/what-is-amazon-relay/) and the [carrier requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## How is the Amazon Relay performance score calculated?

Amazon Relay scores four metrics: on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free. Your overall performance score equals the lowest of those four. Amazon says a carrier is only as good as its lowest metric, so one weak area sets your grade no matter how strong the other three are.

Here is what each metric measures and what pulls it down:

| Metric | What Amazon measures | What hurts it |
|---|---|---|
| On-time | Share of loads that arrive by the planned time at origin and destination, measured from the check-in timestamp | Late arrivals at pickup or delivery, late check-ins |
| Acceptance | How often you reject (cancel) loads you booked, including expired loads | Cancelling booked loads, letting loads expire, cancelling close to pickup (the closer to pickup, the bigger the penalty) |
| App usage | Whether drivers follow the rules for the Relay mobile app on Amazon loads | Closing the app or turning off location services during a trip |
| Disruption-free | Interruptions in transit | Stationary trailers, loads with no assigned driver |

## Why does one bad metric drag down the whole grade?

Because the overall score is the lowest of the four metrics, not an average. A carrier with near-perfect on-time, acceptance and disruption-free numbers still gets graded on whatever its weakest metric is. Fixing your strongest area does nothing for the grade. Fixing the weakest one is the only move that raises it.

Picture it with made-up numbers. Your trucks hit every appointment, you never cancel, and nothing sits stationary. Those three metrics look great. But one driver keeps closing the Relay app mid-trip, and your app usage number lands well below the rest. Your score is now your app usage number. All that on-time work doesn't show up in the grade at all.

That changes how you manage it:

- Find your lowest metric first. That number is your score.
- Fix the habit behind it with the driver or dispatcher who owns it.
- Watch the daily prediction (below) to see if the fix is moving the number.

## What does each Amazon Relay grade open?

Every grade keeps load board access, Relay Rewards eligibility and Post A Truck, with higher grades getting priority matching on Post A Truck. From there, freight opens up by grade: C+ for auctions, B for new contracts, and B+ or higher for early access to new spot loads. Amazon lays this out in its grades guide.

| Grade | What it opens |
|---|---|
| All grades (F to A+) | Load board access, Relay Rewards eligibility, Post A Truck (higher grades get priority matching) |
| C+ and above | Freight auctions for high-demand routes (reefer auctions require B) |
| B and above | Access to book new contracts |
| A+ and A | Contract price alerts |
| A+, A and B+ | Early access to new spot loads |

A few details matter here:

- **Auctions** also depend on equipment count, tenure and CARB compliance, not just grade.
- **Contracts** can be lost. Carriers can lose booked contracts if they drop below C+.
- **Spot loads** appear on the [load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) at staggered times based on grade. A lower grade can mean you see a load after higher-graded carriers already had their shot at it. That's one reason your board can look thinner than another carrier's, covered in [why the load board isn't showing loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board-not-showing-loads/).

## How does the scorecard affect Relay Rewards?

Amazon evaluates your Relay Rewards tier monthly, on the 5th. It uses your company's lowest score from the previous month, plus the miles you drove last month and your tenure. Everyone starts at Basic, and the program is US only. So a bad week can follow you into next month's tier.

Amazon explains the tiers on its [Relay Rewards page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-carriers-save-with-relay-rewards). The key point for your scorecard: Rewards uses the lowest score from the month, not your average or your final week.

## Can you see your Amazon Relay score before it changes?

Yes. Amazon Relay gives carriers a daily prediction of their upcoming score in their account, plus weekly performance trends. Check the prediction daily so a slipping metric shows up before it becomes your grade. It's the earliest warning you get that a driver habit or a disrupted load is costing you.

A simple routine:

1. Open the daily prediction each morning.
2. Note which metric is lowest and whether it moved.
3. If it dropped, find the load behind it while the details are fresh.
4. Decide right away whether that load is worth disputing.

## How do you dispute an Amazon Relay performance score impact?

Carriers can dispute a performance score impact when something happens in transit. You file the dispute in your Relay account, and Amazon decides the outcome. Amazon does not publish a step-by-step procedure or a deadline for scorecard disputes, so file as soon as you spot the impact, while your records are complete.

Before you file, pull together evidence that shows what actually happened on that load:

- **Check-in times.** On-time is measured from the check-in timestamp, so your record of when the driver checked in is the first thing to pull.
- **App and location records.** App usage depends on the app running and location services staying on. Anything showing the app stayed active helps.
- **Messages with Relay.** Any contact with Relay support about the load, including delays you reported as they happened.
- **Photos.** Gate lines, closed docks, road closures, equipment problems at pickup.
- **Documents.** Bills of lading, gate receipts, anything with a time stamp on it.

Then write it up plainly: the load, the impact you're disputing, what happened, and the evidence that shows it. Keep it short and factual.

One thing that trips carriers up: the 30-day dispute window Amazon lists applies to pay disputes, not scorecard impacts. Don't assume you have 30 days on a score dispute.

## What does Amazon not publish about the scorecard?

Amazon does not publish the exact score that maps to each letter grade, how long a single violation stays on your score, a deadline for scorecard disputes, or dispute success rates. Anyone quoting precise cutoffs or win rates is guessing. Work from what Amazon does publish: the four metrics, the lowest-metric rule and the six-week window.

What you can rely on: the six-week window means a bad stretch rolls off as you haul clean loads. Ten or more loads in six active weeks keeps you graded. And the lowest metric is always the one to fix.

## How can NudoIQ help with scorecard disputes?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for the Amazon Relay load board, and it includes a dispute letter tool. It reads your scorecard, identifies the violation behind the score, and drafts a letter that cites Amazon policy. You review it, edit it and submit it yourself. Amazon decides every outcome, and NudoIQ can't promise one.

What it saves you is the writing. Instead of starting from a blank page at the end of a long day, you get a draft built from your own scorecard that you can check against your evidence and send. One carrier, Futo, wrote on the Chrome Web Store: "Their performance dispute feature is a life saver."

The same extension also handles the board side: [auto refresh](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/), booking rules with a profit floor and a cap in the [auto booker](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/), and lane rate history.

NudoIQ is $49.99 a month for every feature ([see pricing](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing)). Start with a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. It's rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is a good Amazon Relay scorecard grade?
Grades run from F to A+. C+ opens freight auctions, B opens new contracts, and B+, A and A+ get early access to new spot loads. Amazon does not publish the exact percentage behind each letter.

### How long does a late load stay on my Amazon Relay scorecard?
Amazon does not publish how long a single violation stays. The score reflects your last six weeks of hauls, so older loads stop counting as they fall out of that window.

### How many loads do I need for an Amazon Relay grade?
You become eligible for a grade after completing ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks. Below that, you don't get a letter grade.

### Does cancelling a load hurt my Amazon Relay score?
Yes. Cancelled and expired loads count against your acceptance metric, and the closer the cancellation is to pickup time, the bigger the penalty. If acceptance becomes your lowest metric, it becomes your score.

### Can I lose an Amazon Relay contract because of my score?
Yes. Amazon says carriers can lose booked contracts if they drop below C+. Booking new contracts requires B or above.

### Is there a deadline to dispute an Amazon Relay scorecard impact?
Amazon does not publish one. The 30-day window it lists is for pay disputes. File a score dispute in your Relay account as soon as you see the impact.

# Amazon Relay Auto Refresh: Why It Matters and How It Works

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: An Amazon Relay auto refresh tool reloads the load board for you every few seconds, so new loads show up without you clicking reload. Good loads often book within seconds. NudoIQ's refresher sets an interval from 1 to 5 seconds, adds up to 20% random jitter, and keeps the board tab from going idle.

## Why Refreshing the Load Board Matters

[Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) the load board auto-refreshes new spot freight matches every 30 seconds. Good loads can book within seconds, so many carriers reload faster than that to see new loads sooner. Manually refreshing every 30 seconds is impractical if you're driving, eating, or managing your business. You step away for five minutes and miss dozens of refreshes. In those five minutes, good loads can post and disappear.

Carriers who want to stay competitive refresh constantly. The faster you refresh, the faster you see loads before other carriers do. A refresher extension automates this, reloading the board every few seconds without you lifting a finger. This is why [refresher and auto-booker extensions](https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/) exist: to keep you in the competition without requiring constant attention.

## Manual Refreshing: The Old Way

Before refresher extensions became standard, carriers had two choices: sit at the computer and hit reload repeatedly, or miss loads. Some carriers sat at their desk hitting F5 or Ctrl+R for hours, watching for loads.

Manually refreshing every 30 seconds means you see new loads 30 seconds after they post (on average 15 seconds, assuming they post mid-cycle). It means you miss the loads that post between your refreshes. It means you're tethered to your computer if you want to compete for the best work.

It also means you're one of many carriers refreshing at roughly the same time.

## What a Refresher Extension Does

A refresher extension automates the reload. You set an interval (how many seconds between refreshes) and the extension does it for you. Instead of manually refreshing every 30 seconds, the extension refreshes every 2 seconds, or 3 seconds, or whatever you choose.

The benefits are obvious:

1. **You see loads faster.** A 2-second refresh means you see loads on average 1 second after they post. A 30-second refresh means you see them 15 seconds later. In that gap, another carrier can book the load.

2. **You don't have to watch.** The extension reloads in the background while you do other things. You're not glued to the screen.

3. **Alerts notify you.** The refresher can ping you when a load matching your rules posts, so you don't have to scan the board manually.

4. **Autobook handles it.** If you set it to Autobook and your rules match, the extension books for you automatically. You don't even have to be at your computer.

## Interval and Jitter Explained

The **interval** is how often the board reloads. A 1-second interval means the board reloads every second. A 5-second interval means every five seconds. Faster intervals mean you see loads sooner, but they also mean more server load and more battery drain on your device.

Pick the interval that fits how hard you're competing. Some carriers go to 1 second if they're trying to catch premium lanes. The tradeoff: faster intervals catch loads faster but hit the server harder and drain your battery quicker.

**Jitter** is random variation added to the interval. Instead of reloading at exactly 2 seconds, 4 seconds, 6 seconds (every 2 seconds), the extension reloads at 2.1 seconds, 4.3 seconds, 5.8 seconds. The variation is tiny (usually up to 20% of the interval) but enough to keep many carriers from hitting the server at exactly the same moment.

Without jitter, every carrier's extension reloads at 2:00, 2:02, 2:04, creating a spike of requests every two seconds. The server gets hammered. With jitter, refreshes spread out: some at 2:00, some at 2:01, some at 2:02, smoothing the load on the server.

Think of it like traffic: if everyone leaves work at 5 p.m., the highway backs up. If people leave at 4:50, 5:00, 5:10, traffic flows. Jitter does the same for the server.

## What Interval Should You Set?

It depends on your goals and your hardware:

**For catching competitive loads (tractor/reefer on busy lanes)**: Use a 1 to 3 second interval. You'll see loads within seconds of posting. Your battery will drain faster and your device will work harder, but you'll catch good loads before other carriers.

**For moderate competition (box truck, less busy lanes)**: Use a 3 to 5 second interval. You'll see loads within a few seconds. It's a good balance between speed and resource use.

**If you're away from the truck**: Use a longer interval if you're not actively booking, or turn off refreshing entirely and set it to Alert mode: notify you when a load posts that matches your rules, and you'll decide whether to book.

**If battery life matters**: Longer intervals use less battery. Shorter intervals use more because your processor is reloading constantly.

## Alerts vs. Auto-Booking

A refresher can work in different modes:

**Alert Mode**: The extension refreshes the board and pings you when a load matching your rules posts. You get a notification (NudoIQ sends Telegram alerts) and then decide whether to book. This is low-friction, you're in control, but it requires you to respond quickly.

**Search Mode**: The extension refreshes the board and highlights (visually marks) loads that match your rules. You scan the board, see the highlights, and click Book if you want. This is also low-friction but requires you to be looking at the board.

**Autobook Mode**: The extension refreshes the board, finds loads matching your rules, and books them automatically. You set your rules once (lane, price, profit floor, max-books cap) and the extension does the booking. You get a notification that it booked something, and you review what it booked. This is hands-off but requires careful rule-setting to avoid booking loads you didn't want.

You can mix these. Some carriers have Autobook running on certain lanes they always want, and Alert mode on others where they want to decide case-by-case.

## Setting Up Your Refresher

To use a refresher extension, you typically:

1. Install it from the Chrome Web Store.
2. Sign in (or it uses your existing Relay login).
3. Set your refresh interval (1 to 5 seconds, depending on how aggressive you want to be).
4. Set your booking rules: lanes, price ranges, distance, equipment type, profit floor, and max-books cap.
5. Set up alerts (NudoIQ uses Telegram).
6. Leave it running.

Most refreshers add a control bar or popup to the Relay load board tab. You can adjust your rules and interval anytime without restarting.

## What Gets Refreshed

The refresher reloads the entire load board: all available loads, all filters, everything. Every refresh shows you what's newly posted and what's still available from earlier refreshes.

Once a load books (gets taken by any carrier), it disappears from the board. The refresher can't book a load that's already gone. If two carriers see the same load and both try to book it at nearly the same moment, the first one wins. This is why interval matters: a faster refresher sees loads sooner and books before slower refreshers do.

## How Refreshers Handle Server Load

Modern refreshers (including NudoIQ) include built-in protections to avoid overwhelming the server:

- **Jitter**: Random variation in the interval prevents synchronized requests.
- **Rate limiting**: Some tools wait a minimum time between refreshes even if you set a faster interval, to prevent abuse.
- **Your account, your responsibility**: The carrier is responsible for its Relay account and for following Relay's terms. Read them before you run any extension.

## The Role of Refreshing in Your Strategy

Refreshing is the foundation. [Booking rules](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/), [profit calculation](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/), and [rate history](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) add layers on top, but refreshing (fast, steady, consistent) is what gets you first look at loads.

If your refresher runs on a 2-second interval and your competitor's runs on a 30-second interval (or no interval at all), you'll see loads before they do. That's the advantage.

## NudoIQ's Refresh Approach

NudoIQ's refresher lets you set the interval from 1 to 5 seconds with built-in jitter (up to 20% random variation per interval). The extension keeps the Relay tab from going idle and refreshes on schedule, even if you're not looking at it.

It doesn't just refresh: it runs alongside [Lane Intelligence](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) (showing rate history) and [Net Profit calculation](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) (showing what you keep), and it integrates with [Autobook](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) so you can set rules once and let it book automatically.

The extension is 5.0 rated on the Chrome Web Store and runs on desktop Chrome in English and Spanish. It costs $49.99 a month for every feature, with a 7-day free trial (no card needed to start) so you can test the refresh and see what the rate history and profit tools do.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a 1-second refresh interval too aggressive?
A 1-second refresh is the fastest setting NudoIQ offers and uses the most battery. If you're competing for loads on busy lanes, it helps you see new loads sooner. If you're not in a hurry, 2 to 5 seconds is plenty.

### Will my extension's refresh get me kicked off Relay?
Nobody can promise that, and we won't. The carrier is responsible for its Relay account and for following Relay's terms, so read them before you run any extension.

### Do I need to leave my browser window open for the refresher to work?
Yes, your browser window (or at least the tab with the Relay load board) needs to stay open. The refresher runs inside that tab. If you close the browser or the tab, the refresher stops.

### Can I set different refresh intervals for different times of day?
Most refreshers don't have built-in scheduling, so you'd have to change the interval manually. Some carriers who compete hard in the morning but less at night might set a 2-second interval at 5 a.m. and drop it to 5 seconds at 2 p.m. You can do this, but it's manual.

### What if I set the interval too fast and it drains my battery?
Stop the refresher, set a longer interval, or plug in your device. A 1 to 2 second interval on a laptop uses noticeable power. A 3 to 5 second interval is more balanced.

### Can a refresher book loads when I'm offline?
No. The refresher runs inside your browser in real-time. If your internet drops, the refresher stops and can't reload the board. Once you're back online, it resumes.

### Do I need an alert notification to book a load?
Not if you're using Autobook. The extension will book for you automatically based on your rules, and then notify you that it booked something. If you're using Alert or Search mode, you have to respond to the notification or notice the highlighted load yourself.

# Amazon Relay Auto Booker: How Automatic Booking Works

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: An Amazon Relay auto booker is a browser extension that books loads matching rules you set, such as lane, price and profit. Every booking is the carrier's commitment, so guardrails matter: a profit floor, a max-books cap and testing rules in alert mode first. Cancelling booked loads hurts the acceptance score.

## What an Auto-Booker Does

An auto-booker extension (also called an autobooker or auto-book tool) refreshes the Relay load board constantly and books loads that match the rules you set. You don't have to click Book. The extension does it automatically.

Example: You set rules that say "book any load from Portland to Eugene for $400 or more, if the profit is at least $150 after costs." When a load matching those criteria posts, the extension sees it and books it for you. You get a notification that it booked something, and you review what you got.

The advantage is obvious: you can act on loads faster, and you're not glued to the screen. The risk is equally obvious: without good guardrails, you can book loads that don't work for your operation.

## The Risk of Unintended Bookings

The biggest mistake carriers make with auto-bookers is setting rules that are too loose. Set a rule that says "book any load over $200" and you might book a 200-mile haul at $2 per mile (which nets you nothing after costs). Set a rule that says "book anything from Oregon" and you might book a load that goes to California, adding six hours you didn't plan.

Auto-bookers book fast and without mercy. If your rules match, they book. No "wait, let me think about this." No second-guessing. If you set the rules wrong, you'll book loads you didn't want.

This is why guardrails matter. The best auto-bookers make it hard to book the wrong load.

## Essential Guardrails: Rules, Profit Floor, and Max-Books Cap

A good auto-booker includes three kinds of rules:

**Booking Rules**: Filter the loads the extension will consider. You can specify:
- **Lane**: Only book loads from Portland to Eugene. Don't book Portland to Los Angeles.
- **Price Range**: Only book loads between $300 and $600. Don't book anything cheaper or more expensive.
- **Distance**: Only book loads up to 500 miles. Skip loads that are too long.
- **Load Type**: Book only dry van. Skip refrigerated or container loads if you don't have that equipment.
- **Pickup Time**: Only book loads that pick up between 6 a.m. and 4 p.m. Avoid overnight pickups you're not prepared for.

Booking rules narrow the field. They say "of all the loads on the board, only consider these ones."

**Profit Floor**: Set a minimum profit the extension must see before it books. Example: "Don't book anything that nets less than $150 after subtracting driver pay, fuel, maintenance, and deadhead."

A profit floor is your second line of defense. Even if a load matches your lane, price, and distance rules, the extension checks the net profit. If it doesn't clear the floor, no book.

**Max-Books Cap**: Set a maximum number of loads the extension will book per day or per week. Example: "Stop booking after you've booked 5 loads today."

The max-books cap is your third line of defense. It prevents you from overbooking and running out of drivers. Once you hit the cap, the extension stops booking for that period, even if perfect loads post.

Together, these three guardrails protect you from booking loads you didn't intend.

## The Three Modes: Alert, Search, Autobook

Different auto-booker extensions offer different modes:

**Alert Mode**: The extension refreshes the board and notifies you when a load matches your rules. You get a Telegram alert with details about the load. You decide whether to book. You stay in control but have to respond quickly, because other carriers might book the same load while you're thinking.

Alert mode is good when you want to be involved in the decision but don't want to stare at the board. It's also good for testing your rules before you turn on Autobook: use Alert mode first, see what loads it suggests, and verify they're the right ones.

**Search Mode**: The extension refreshes the board and highlights loads that match your rules. You scan the board, see the highlighted loads, and click Book if you want. You stay in control and can visually inspect a load before booking. But you have to be looking at the board, and other carriers might book the load while you're reading it.

Search mode is good when you want to make the final decision but want the extension to do the scanning for you. It's also good for less time-sensitive work: if you're not in a race to be first, you can look and decide.

**Autobook Mode**: The extension refreshes the board, finds loads matching your rules, and books them automatically. The extension handles the booking; you don't have to be there. You get a notification that it booked something.

Autobook mode is the most hands-off but requires the most confidence in your rules. You need to trust that your lane, price, distance, profit floor, and max-books rules will produce bookings you want.

## Setting Your Booking Rules Safely

To use Autobook safely, follow this process:

**Step 1: Define Your Operation**
- What lanes do I actually run? (e.g., Portland to Eugene, Portland to Seattle, Portland to Los Angeles)
- What's my minimum profit per load? (e.g., $150 net)
- What's my maximum distance? (e.g., 400 miles)
- What's my maximum number of drivers available? (e.g., 5, so I'll book 5 loads max per day)

Write these down. They're the foundation of your rules.

**Step 2: Start with Alert Mode**
- Set your lane, price, and distance rules in Alert mode.
- Let it run for a day or two.
- When it alerts you, read the load and ask: "Would I have booked this?"
- If yes, great. If no, adjust your rule.

Alert mode is a testing ground. Use it to verify your rules produce the loads you want.

**Step 3: Add a Profit Floor**
- Once your lane/price/distance rules look good, set a profit floor.
- Example: don't book anything under $150 net.
- Let it run another day.
- Again, ask: "Is it suggesting loads I'd actually take?"

**Step 4: Set a Max-Books Cap**
- Decide how many loads you can handle per day. (Don't overbuild.)
- Set the cap to that number.
- Example: cap at 5 loads per day.

**Step 5: Try Autobook**
- Once you're confident in your rules, switch to Autobook.
- Let it run and watch what it books.
- In the first day or two, check that it's making the right decisions.
- If it books something you don't want, adjust the rule that allowed it.

This progression, Alert → Search → Autobook, lets you test your rules before automation takes over. The common mistake is jumping straight to Autobook. Taking time to verify the rules in Alert mode costs no money and saves headaches later.

## What Autobook Actually Books

When you're running Autobook and a load matches your rules, the extension clicks Book for you. It submits the booking through the board, just as if you had clicked.

From Amazon's perspective, you booked the load. It's your obligation. You accepted it. If you can't take it later, cancelling hits your acceptance score, and the closer to pickup, the bigger the penalty.

This is why profit floor and max-books cap are non-negotiable. If you set a bad rule and the extension books 10 loads you can't handle, you cancel most of them and your scorecard suffers.

## Instant Book: One-Click Booking

Some extensions (including NudoIQ) offer an Instant Book feature: a button on the load card that books the load in one click, instead of the multi-step flow (find load, read details, click Book, fill shipping info, confirm).

Instant Book isn't automatic, you still click the button manually, but it's faster than the standard booking flow. You see a load, check it's good, and hit Instant Book instead of navigating menus.

## Common Autobook Mistakes

**Mistake 1: Too-Loose Rules**
Setting rules that are too broad ("book any load over $100" or "book anything from California") leads to unwanted bookings. Start narrow and widen only after testing.

**Mistake 2: No Profit Floor**
A $500 rate sounds good until you realize it nets $50 after paying your driver and fuel. Always set a profit floor.

**Mistake 3: No Max-Books Cap**
Without a cap, the extension books loads all day, and you run out of drivers or time. Set a cap to match your actual capacity.

**Mistake 4: Not Testing in Alert Mode First**
Jumping straight to Autobook without testing your rules is asking for trouble. Use Alert mode first. See what it suggests. Verify it's the right stuff. Then automate.

**Mistake 5: Setting a Cap Too High**
"I'll book 20 loads a day" sounds ambitious until you realize you only have 5 drivers. Be realistic about your capacity and set your cap accordingly.

## How NudoIQ's Autobook Works

NudoIQ's control bar includes three modes: Alert (pings you), Search (highlights matches), and Autobook (books automatically). You set price and lane rules, a profit floor, and a max-books cap.

The extension uses [Net Profit calculation](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) to check whether a load clears your profit floor. So you're not just setting a dollar target: you're setting a profit target after costs.

[Instant Book](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) is one click on the load card. Telegram alerts notify you when the extension books something, so you know immediately what was booked.

If you're unsure about your rules, start in Alert mode and let NudoIQ suggest loads for a day. See if the suggestions are good. Then switch to Autobook.

## Setting a Profit Floor in NudoIQ

When you set a profit floor in NudoIQ, you're saying "don't book anything that nets less than $X per load after subtracting driver pay, fuel, maintenance, and deadhead to pickup."

Example:
- Posted rate: $600
- Driver pay: $150
- Fuel: $100
- Maintenance: $50
- Deadhead to pickup: $50
- Net profit: $600 - $150 - $100 - $50 - $50 = $250

If your profit floor is $150, this load clears it. If your floor is $300, it doesn't. NudoIQ calculates this for every load, so your Autobook rule respects the floor automatically.

## When NOT to Use Autobook

Don't use Autobook if:

- You're not sure about your rules yet. Test in Alert mode first.
- Your operation changes frequently (different lanes, different equipment). Manual booking gives you more control.
- You're in a learning phase and don't yet know what works for you. Autobook is powerful once you know your business.
- You have unreliable internet. If your connection drops while a load is booking, it might book but you might not know.

Use Alert mode or Search mode as long as you need to. There's no shame in manual booking while you're learning.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I set different booking rules for different times of day?
Most auto-bookers don't have built-in scheduling. You'd have to change your rules manually if you want to book different loads at different times. Some carriers adjust their profit floor during slow hours (willing to take lower margin loads when work is scarce) but keep it higher during busy hours. You can do this, but it's manual.

### What happens if I set my max-books cap too low?
You'll stop getting bookings after you hit the cap, even if perfect loads post. If you cap at 2 loads a day and the board is flooded with great work, you'll miss it after your 2 are booked. Set a cap based on your actual capacity, and review it regularly.

### How do I adjust my profit floor if my costs change?
Most auto-bookers let you change your profit floor anytime. If your fuel costs drop or your driver pay changes, update the floor and the extension respects the new number immediately.

### What if the extension books a load and I want to cancel it?
You can cancel a booked load, but it counts against your tender-acceptance score on your Relay scorecard. Cancel if you absolutely have to, but do it sparingly. This is why testing your rules in Alert mode first matters: fewer bad bookings means fewer cancellations.

### Can Autobook book loads when I'm offline?
No. The extension runs inside your browser. If your device is off or your internet is down, the extension can't refresh the board or book loads. It only works when your browser is open and online.

### Is booking via extension as reliable as booking manually?
The extension books through the same board you use. Any booking it makes is yours, so set your rules carefully.

### Can I use Autobook on multiple trucks at the same time?
Yes. You can have NudoIQ running on multiple devices and multiple load board tabs. Just remember: if two devices/tabs are both running Autobook with the same rules, they might both try to book the same load, which could cause issues. Consider running Autobook on one device and Alert/Search mode on others.

# Best Amazon Relay Extensions: Refresher and Auto-Booker Tools

URL: https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: The main Amazon Relay extensions are LoadFetcher and Rocket Relay, which offer free tiers focused on refreshing and booking, plus smaller tools like SwiftRelay and FlashRelay. NudoIQ costs $49.99 a month and adds lane rate history, net profit per load and scorecard dispute letters. Compare refresh control, booking guardrails, rate data and support.

## Why You Need a Relay Extension

The Amazon Relay load board refreshes when you reload it. Good loads book within seconds. Manual refreshing every 30 seconds isn't practical if you're driving, managing dispatch, or running your business. An extension automates the reload and notifies you or books loads for you, so you don't have to watch the screen.

Besides the bigger names, there are a dozen or so smaller refreshers in the category. Understanding what to look for helps you pick the right one.

## What to Look For in a Relay Extension

**Refresh Control**: Can you set the interval (how often it reloads) and does it add jitter (random variation to prevent server strain)? A good refresher lets you choose 1 to 5 second intervals and includes built-in jitter so every refresh isn't at the exact same moment.

**Booking Rules**: Can you set rules to book only certain loads? Look for the ability to filter by lane, price range, load type, distance, and equipment. A tool that books only loads matching your criteria is safer than one that books indiscriminately.

**Profit Floor and Max-Books Cap**: Does it let you set a minimum profit and a maximum number of books? These guardrails protect you from booking loads you didn't intend to take. A profit floor means "don't book anything below $X net profit." A max-books cap means "stop booking once I've booked 5 loads today."

**Rate Data and Decision Support**: Does it show you lane history, net profit per load, or other rate context? Or does it just notify you when a load posts and let you decide? Tools that surface rate data help you make faster decisions.

**Alerts**: Can it notify you when a load matching your rules posts? NudoIQ sends Telegram alerts, which reach your phone.

**Data Handling and Privacy**: Where does your data go? Some tools store booking rules on your computer only. Others upload to a server. Ask yourself: do I want my lane preferences, profit targets, and booking history on someone else's server?

**Updates and Support**: Is the tool actively maintained? An extension that hasn't been updated in months might break when Chrome or Relay changes. Look for tools with recent updates and a way to report problems.

**Cost**: Free tools exist. Paid tools add more features. Decide whether the features are worth the cost for your operation.

## The Top Extensions

### LoadFetcher

LoadFetcher is the largest Amazon Relay extension by installs. It offers a free refresher tier and is focused on refreshing and booking.

What's advertised: refreshing and booking. What's not advertised: lane rate history, net profit per load, or scorecard dispute letters.

LoadFetcher's pitch is simplicity and cost: a free refresher tier. If that's all you need, the free tier may be enough.

**Best for**: Carriers who want a refresher and basic booker, nothing more, and prefer not to pay.

### Rocket Relay and Rocket Pro

Rocket Relay is a refresher and booker with a free tier. Its core pitch is that your business data stays on your own computer. It's focused on refreshing and booking.

**Best for**: Carriers who want a free refresher and booker and prioritize keeping their data local.

### SwiftRelay and FlashRelay

Several smaller refreshers exist (SwiftRelay, FlashRelay, and others) that focus on the core functionality: refreshing and booking.

**Best for**: Carriers who want a basic refresher.

### NudoIQ

NudoIQ is a browser extension that runs inside the Relay load board and includes every feature in one monthly subscription: $49.99/month after a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start.

**Refresh Control**: Slider sets the interval from 1 to 5 seconds with built-in jitter.

**Three Booking Modes**: Alert (pings you on a match), Search (highlights matching loads visually), Autobook (books automatically if your rules match). Set price and lane rules, a profit floor, and a max-books cap.

**Lane Intelligence**: For each load, NudoIQ shows the 90-day rate history for that lane, a target rate, an expected range, and a confidence level. Example: "$483 target next to a $407 board price." This is decision support, not a guarantee: Amazon rates change based on season, time of day, volume, and other factors.

**Net Profit Per Load**: Instead of just the posted rate, NudoIQ calculates the dollars you keep after subtracting driver pay, fuel, maintenance, and deadhead to pickup. You see the net profit and net $/mile for every load.

**Scorecard Dispute Drafting**: NudoIQ reads your Relay scorecard, identifies the violation, and drafts a dispute letter citing Amazon policy. You review, edit, and submit. Amazon makes the final decision.

**Backhaul Finder**: Search for loads from your current drop-off back toward home within your radius and time window. Sort by total pay, rate per mile, pickup time, or distance home.

**Post A Truck Helper**: When posting availability, NudoIQ shows origin, destination, distance, and board price alongside your minimums, then posts with one click.

**Other Features**: HOS overview, driver dispatch by text/email on assignment, Telegram alerts.

**Best for**: Carriers who want a full-featured refresher, rate history, profit calculation, dispute support, and backhaul finding all in one tool.

A good extension for you is one that:

1. **Automates what you do manually**: If you refresh constantly, it should refresh for you. If you struggle to judge rates, it should show you rate history.

2. **Includes guardrails**: Set a profit floor, set a max-books cap, and the tool respects those limits so you don't accidentally book unprofitable work.

3. **Stays updated**: Recent updates mean the developers are actively maintaining it and fixing issues.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I use two refresher extensions at the same time?
Technically you can, but it's not recommended. Two extensions both trying to refresh the board and book loads can cause conflicts, duplicate bookings, or unexpected behavior. Pick one extension and stick with it.

### Do I need a separate account to use a Relay extension?
It depends on the extension, so check each one before you install. NudoIQ asks for your email address when you start the free trial, and you activate the extension with a code sent to that email. After that, it runs in your own Chrome browser, inside your signed-in Relay tab, and never asks for your Amazon password.

### How fast do these extensions book loads?
An extension in Autobook mode books as soon as it sees a matching load on a refresh, without you reading and clicking. How soon it sees the load depends on your refresh interval. No tool can promise you'll get a load first.

### What if an extension books a load I didn't want?
Set a profit floor and max-books cap. These are your primary defenses. A profit floor means the extension won't book loads that don't clear your minimum profit. A max-books cap means it stops booking once you've booked, say, 5 loads. Together, they prevent unwanted bookings.

### Is NudoIQ's lane rate history always accurate?
Lane rate history in NudoIQ comes from the Relay load board's posted rates over 90 days. It's historical fact, not a prediction. But Amazon rates change based on season, time of day, volume, and other factors, so past rates don't guarantee today's rate. That's why NudoIQ calls it decision support: it helps you judge whether today's rate is high or low, but you still decide whether to take it.

# LoadFetcher vs NudoIQ: What's the Difference

URL: https://nudoiq.com/loadfetcher-alternative/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: NudoIQ is a LoadFetcher alternative for Amazon Relay. Both refresh the load board and book loads, and LoadFetcher offers a free refresher tier. NudoIQ costs $49.99 a month after a 7-day free trial with no card needed to start, and adds lane rate history, net profit per load, scorecard dispute letters, a backhaul finder and a Post A Truck helper.

## What Both Tools Do

LoadFetcher and NudoIQ are both Amazon Relay extensions. They both live in your browser, run on desktop Chrome, and do the same core job: refresh the load board automatically so you don't have to, and book matching loads for you if you set it up.

That's the table-stakes feature set for any Relay extension. The load board refreshes when you reload it, good loads book within seconds, and manual refreshing every 30 seconds doesn't work if you're actually driving or managing your business. A refresher extension solves that.

Both tools refresh the board and book loads. NudoIQ also lets you set booking rules (lane, price, distance, equipment), a profit floor (the minimum net you'll accept) and a max-books cap (stop booking once you hit it). LoadFetcher doesn't advertise a profit floor or a cap.

## Where LoadFetcher Stops

LoadFetcher's pitch is simplicity. It offers a free refresher tier and focuses on refreshing and booking. If that's all you need, the free version may cover it.

LoadFetcher does not advertise lane rate history (what that route normally pays), net profit per load (what you keep after costs), scorecard dispute letters, backhaul finding, or Post A Truck helpers. Those features are not part of LoadFetcher's public offering.

For a carrier who wants a refresher and basic booker, LoadFetcher's free tier is a zero-dollar way to work smarter than manual refreshing.

## Where NudoIQ Adds

NudoIQ starts where LoadFetcher's free tier ends. Every feature is included at one price: $49.99 a month.

**Lane Intelligence**: NudoIQ checks the posted rate against that lane's 90-day price history. It shows you a target rate (what the lane normally pays), an expected range, and a confidence level. You see, for example, "$483 target next to a $407 board price." This is decision support, not a guarantee (Amazon sets rates based on season, time of day, volume, and other factors) but it tells you whether today's rate is high or low for that specific route.

The extension calculates this for every load card, so you can set a profit floor and hide loads that don't clear it. A $600 rate might net $200 after costs on one lane and $400 on another. NudoIQ shows you the actual take-home.

**Scorecard Dispute Letters**: Amazon grades carriers on on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free, and your overall score is the lowest of the four (see our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/)). Low grades limit your access to loads. If Amazon dings your scorecard and you disagree with the violation, NudoIQ reads your scorecard, identifies the violation, and drafts a dispute letter citing Amazon policy. You review it, edit it if needed, and submit it yourself. Amazon makes the final decision, but you don't start from a blank page.

It sorts by total pay, rate per mile, pickup time, or distance home, so you can find a profitable return trip quickly instead of scrolling the entire board.

**Post A Truck Helper**: When you post availability on Relay's Post A Truck feature, NudoIQ shows your origin, destination, distance, and board price next to your minimum $/mile and minimum payout. Then it posts with one button.

**Other Conveniences**: HOS overview, driver dispatch by text/email on assignment, control bar with three modes (Alert to ping you on a match, Search to highlight matches, Autobook to book automatically).

### Does NudoIQ slow down the load board?

### What if I use LoadFetcher now and want to switch to NudoIQ?
Remove LoadFetcher from your extensions, then install NudoIQ from the Chrome Web Store. Sign up for the 7-day free trial, and you'll see all the features. Your Relay login and load board stay the same: you're just changing the extension.

### Does NudoIQ tell me which loads to book?
No. It shows you rate history, profit, and dispute data, but the booking decision is yours. NudoIQ is decision support. You set the rules (price, lane, minimum profit), and it alerts you or books automatically based on those rules. Amazon Relay is your business; the tool helps you run it smarter.

### Is there a discount if I sign up for longer than one month?
NudoIQ's pricing is month-to-month at $49.99. There's no annual pricing or discount. You pay for the month and can cancel anytime.

### How do I know if lane rate history is accurate?
Lane rate history in NudoIQ comes from the Relay load board's posted rates over the past 90 days. It's not a prediction: it's what that lane actually paid. But Amazon's rates change based on season, volume, time of day, and other factors, so historical rates don't guarantee today's rate. That's why NudoIQ calls it decision support, not a guarantee.

# Amazon Relay loads: load types, equipment and how to book them

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-loads/
Published: 2026-10-02. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: Amazon Relay loads are posted only on the Amazon Relay load board, which is open 24/7 and free to search and book. Carriers book spot loads (one-way or round trip), reserve blocks, take short-term contracts, bid in auctions or use Post A Truck. Most Relay loads are power only, and higher-graded carriers get first access to new loads.

## Where do Amazon Relay loads come from?

Amazon tenders its Relay loads only through the Amazon Relay load board. It does not post them on third-party load boards. The board is open 24/7, free to search and book, and lists thousands of loads at any time. Volume nearly doubles during peak seasons like Prime Day and the holidays.

Amazon describes the board in its [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board). Each listing shows stop locations, arrival and departure times, the payment breakdown and the load requirements. For how the board itself works, see our [Amazon Relay load board guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/). You need an approved carrier account first, covered in [Amazon Relay requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## What types of loads are on Amazon Relay?

Amazon Relay offers one-way loads, round trips, blocks, spot freight, short-term contracts and auctions. Round trips start and end at the same domicile and usually need only a tractor. One-way loads need a box truck or your own trailer. Blocks reserve your truck and driver for a set time, and contracts book weeks of loads in advance.

Amazon breaks these down in its overview of [trucking work on Relay](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-work-amazon-relay):

| Load type | What it is | Equipment needed |
|---|---|---|
| Round trip | Begins and ends at the same domicile | Usually just a tractor (power only) |
| One-way | A single haul; book backhauls or head hauls to cut deadhead | A box truck or your own trailer |
| Block | A chunk of time you reserve trucks and drivers for Relay, paid even if Amazon doesn't use the full block | Depends on the block |
| Spot | Last-minute loads you book instantly at the listed price | Depends on the load |
| Short-term contract | Full or partial weeks of loads, booked in advance | Depends on the contract; box truck contracts exist |
| Auction | Contracts of up to 6 months, bid in bulk by spreadsheet; the winning rate is locked for the contract | Depends on the lane; most bids need grade C+ or better |

Amazon also lists three driver setups: a 13-hour solo (one day of loads, including 11 hours of drive time), a 37-hour solo (two days, with the 10-hour rest break taken outside base cities), and team (two drivers trading off).

If you want several loads in a row, [how to book multiple loads on Amazon Relay](https://nudoiq.com/how-to-book-multiple-loads-on-amazon-relay/) walks through the options.

## What equipment do you need for Amazon Relay loads?

Most Amazon Relay loads are power only: you bring the tractor and Amazon provides the trailer. Relay also supports 26 ft and 16 ft box trucks with a working tuck-under liftgate, 48 ft and 53 ft dry vans, 53 ft reefers that meet the FDA Sanitary Transportation Rule, and 20, 40 and 45 ft high-cube containers.

Amazon's [truck requirements page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-truck-requirements) says it plainly: "The majority of Amazon Relay loads are power-only." Amazon says hauling its trailers cuts facility wait time and trailer maintenance cost. More on that in our [Amazon Relay power only](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/) page.

The details by equipment:

- **Tractors.** Day cab and sleeper tractors. Power only covers most of the board.
- **Box trucks.** 26 ft and 16 ft, dock height, with a working tuck-under liftgate. Cargo vans can't be used. Box truck contracts exist, including 8-hour and 13-hour solo contracts with round trips. See [Amazon Relay box truck loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck-loads/).
- **Your own trailer.** Needed for one-way loads if you don't run a box truck. 48 ft or 53 ft dry van.
- **Reefer.** 53 ft reefers must meet the FDA Sanitary Transportation Rule.
- **Containers.** 20, 40 and 45 ft high cube, UIIA compliant.

There's no fleet size requirement to haul for Relay. Our [analysis of FMCSA inspection records](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/) found that about 70% of carriers hauling Amazon freight run 1-5 power units.

## How do you get loads on Amazon Relay?

You get loads on Amazon Relay by searching and booking on the load board, posting your truck with Post A Truck, bidding in auctions, or pitching a price through Relay Assistant on eligible urgent loads. Spot loads book at the listed price. Your performance grade decides how early you see new spot loads and which auctions and contracts you can reach.

The four ways in, from Amazon's guide to [setting your own rates](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/3-ways-to-set-your-own-freight-rates-on-amazon-relay):

1. **Load board.** Search, filter and book spot loads at the listed price.
2. **Post A Truck.** Post your equipment and driver availability up to two weeks ahead and set a minimum rate per mile. Available for power only, box truck and live loads.
3. **Auctions.** Bid in bulk on contracts of up to 6 months. Most bids need a C+ grade or better.
4. **Relay Assistant.** On eligible urgent listings, top-performing carriers can pitch a price 24/7. Amazon may counter.

Final rates reflect market conditions in every case.

## How do you book Amazon Relay loads faster?

Good Amazon Relay loads get booked within seconds, so speed comes from setup: tight filters, saved searches, reload suggestions and Post A Truck to get matched before loads reach the board. A strong grade helps too, because high-performing carriers get first access to new loads. Many carriers add a refresher and alerts on top.

**Filters and saved searches.** The board filters by origin and destination or radius, trailer status, equipment type, load type, driver type, maximum stops, trip length, rate range, and pickup and delivery windows. Save your most-used searches so you aren't rebuilding them every time.

**Reload and return-trip suggestions.** The board suggests return trips, replacements for cancelled loads and more loads to keep a driver moving.

**Post A Truck.** Per Amazon's [Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck), you can include or exclude cities, pick one-way or round trip, and set distance or duration limits. A "match outlook" shows High, Medium or Low odds based on the previous six weeks of loads. Matched carriers get first access to freight in their window before it reaches the load board.

**Your grade.** Carriers graded A+, A and B+ get early access to new spot loads, which appear at staggered times by grade. Our [Amazon Relay scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains how to protect it.

**Refreshers and alerts.** The board itself auto-refreshes new matches every 30 seconds, and Amazon offers email alerts and push notifications. Carriers who want faster reloads use an [auto refresh extension](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) or an [auto booker](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) that books loads matching their rules.

## How are Amazon Relay load rates shown?

Every Amazon Relay spot rate is all-in: a base rate, a fuel surcharge that tracks fuel prices, and tolls. You book at the listed price. Distance (including deadhead and trip direction), equipment type, load characteristics like live loads, seasonal demand and regional market conditions all move the rate. Amazon pays weekly.

Amazon covers this in [understanding Relay rates](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates). Pay varies by lane, timing and equipment, so the same lane can pay differently at different hours. To judge whether a rate is worth taking, see [how much Amazon Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

## How can NudoIQ help you catch Amazon Relay loads?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside the Amazon Relay load board in your browser. It refreshes the board every 1 to 5 seconds with random jitter, alerts you or books when a load matches your rules, and shows lane rate history and net profit on each load card. Bookings and rates are never guaranteed.

You set the price and lane rules, a profit floor and a max-books cap, and pick Alert, Search or Autobook. Autobook stops at the cap and the profit floor. Telegram alerts tell you when a load lands. The backhaul finder searches loads from where your current load ends, pointed back toward home.

It's $49.99 a month for every feature, the same for one truck or twenty ([pricing](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing)). Start with a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I find Amazon Relay loads on DAT or other load boards?
No. Amazon tenders Relay loads only through the Amazon Relay load board. Third-party load boards don't carry them.

### What is a block on Amazon Relay?
A block is a chunk of time you reserve your trucks and drivers for Relay. Amazon pays for the block even if it doesn't use the full time.

### Do I need my own trailer for Amazon Relay?
Not for most loads. The majority of Relay loads are power only, where Amazon provides the trailer. One-way loads need a box truck or your own trailer.

### Can I haul Amazon Relay loads with a cargo van?
No. Cargo vans can't be used. The smallest supported equipment is a 16 ft box truck with a working tuck-under liftgate.

### What time do new loads post on Amazon Relay?
The board is open 24/7 with thousands of loads listed at any time. New spot loads appear at staggered times by grade, so A+, A and B+ carriers see them first.

# Amazon Relay carrier data 2026: what FMCSA inspection records show

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/
Published: 2026-10-02. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: A NudoIQ analysis of the FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File found 101,444 roadside inspections listing Amazon as the shipper, across 22,866 distinct carriers (USDOT numbers), from 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22. About 530 new carriers appear each month, and about 70% of carriers hauling Amazon freight run 1-5 power units. Inspections count Amazon freight, not only Amazon Relay loads.

## What are the key findings on Amazon carriers?

We counted public FMCSA roadside inspections that list Amazon as the shipper, queried on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25. An inspection is not a load, so every count here is a floor. Amazon on the bill of lading means Amazon freight, which is not proof the load was booked through Amazon Relay. The main numbers:

- From 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22, 101,444 FMCSA roadside inspections listed Amazon as the shipper, across 22,866 distinct carriers (USDOT numbers).
- About 16,978 carriers had at least one Amazon-shipper inspection from 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-22, and all of them show as active in the FMCSA census.
- Roughly 530 carriers per month show up on an Amazon-shipper inspection for the first time: 3,167 new carriers from 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-22.
- Of 321,311 carriers inspected between 2026-03-22 and 2026-09-22, 7,932 (2.47%, about 1 in 40) had at least one inspection listing Amazon as the shipper.
- Through 2026-09-22, Amazon-shipper inspections in 2026 (29,335) had already reached about 82% of the full 2025 count (35,753).
- About 70% of carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01 run 1-5 power units.
- Of carriers whose last Amazon inspection was 0-3 months before 2026-03-22 and who were inspected again in the next six months, 64.5% were again carrying Amazon freight.

## How many carriers haul Amazon freight?

At least 22,866 distinct carriers (USDOT numbers) appeared on FMCSA roadside inspections listing Amazon as the shipper between 2023-09-24 and 2026-09-22, across 101,444 inspections. In the shorter window from 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-22, about 16,978 carriers had at least one such inspection, and all of them show as active in the FMCSA census.

These are floors, since most loads are never inspected. The counts also include Amazon's own fleets and contract carriers, not only carriers booking on the [Amazon Relay load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/).

Of all 321,311 carriers inspected for any reason between 2026-03-22 and 2026-09-22, 7,932 (2.47%, about 1 in 40) had an Amazon-shipper inspection.

## How fast are new carriers showing up?

About 530 carriers per month show up on an Amazon-shipper inspection for the first time. Counting carriers whose first Amazon-shipper inspection fell in each window: 558 since 2026-08-25 (about 30 days), 1,584 since 2026-07-01 (about 90 days) and 3,167 since 2026-04-01 (about 180 days), all through 2026-09-22.

This chart shows the number of newly seen carriers in each window.
Carriers seen with Amazon freight for the first time:

| Window (ending 2026-09-22) | First-time carriers |
|---|---|
| Last ~30 days (from 2026-08-25) | 558 |
| Last ~90 days (from 2026-07-01) | 1,584 |
| Last ~180 days (from 2026-04-01) | 3,167 |

Source: FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File (fx4q-ay7w): carriers whose first Amazon-shipper inspection falls in the window.
"First seen" means the first time a carrier appears on an Amazon-shipper inspection in the three-year file. Some of these carriers may have hauled Amazon freight earlier without being inspected.

## Is Amazon freight volume growing?

Yes, by inspection count. Amazon-shipper inspections rose from 29,036 in 2024 to 35,753 in 2025. Through 2026-09-22, the 2026 count was 29,335, already about 82% of the full 2025 total. The number of distinct carriers inspected with Amazon freight followed the same direction: 9,652 in 2024, 11,322 in 2025.

This chart shows Amazon-shipper inspections and distinct carriers by year.
Roadside inspections listing Amazon as shipper, by year:

| Year | Inspections | Distinct carriers |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 (Sep 24 to Dec 31) | 7,320 | 3,681 |
| 2024 | 29,036 | 9,652 |
| 2025 | 35,753 | 11,322 |
| 2026 (Jan 1 to Sep 22) | 29,335 | 10,117 |

Source: FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File (fx4q-ay7w), inspections where the shipper name contains AMAZON.
Read 2023 and 2026 as partial years. The 2023 figures (7,320 inspections, 3,681 carriers) start on 2023-09-24, and 2026 (29,335 inspections, 10,117 carriers) runs through 2026-09-22. Inspection counts are an indirect signal of freight volume, not a direct measure of it.

## Where are Amazon carriers based?

California leads by a wide margin, with 3,011 carriers that had an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01, by physical address. Ohio (1,689) and Illinois (1,589) come next, ahead of Pennsylvania (1,155) and Texas (972). Ohio and Illinois ranking above Texas is something a general carrier list would not show.

This chart shows the top 12 states by number of carriers.
Carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01, top 12 home states:

| State | Carriers |
|---|---|
| California | 3,011 |
| Ohio | 1,689 |
| Illinois | 1,589 |
| Pennsylvania | 1,155 |
| Texas | 972 |
| Florida | 903 |
| Minnesota | 709 |
| Washington | 653 |
| New Jersey | 568 |
| North Carolina | 449 |
| Georgia | 404 |
| Michigan | 358 |

Source: Carrier physical state from the FMCSA Company Census (az4n-8mr2), joined on USDOT number.
After Texas come Florida (903), Minnesota (709), Washington (653), New Jersey (568), North Carolina (449), Georgia (404) and Michigan (358). State is the carrier's physical address in the FMCSA census, not where the inspection happened.

## How big are the carriers that haul Amazon freight?

Most are small. About 70% of carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01 run 1-5 power units. The single largest group is 1-2 power units, with 9,941 carriers. At the other end, 72 carriers run more than 1,000 power units.

This chart shows carriers by fleet size (power units).
Fleet size (power units) of carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01:

| Power units | Carriers | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | 9,941 | 51.4% |
| 3-5 | 3,600 | 18.6% |
| 6-10 | 1,933 | 10.0% |
| 11-20 | 1,276 | 6.6% |
| 21-50 | 1,333 | 6.9% |
| 51-100 | 641 | 3.3% |
| 101-1,000 | 559 | 2.9% |
| 1,000+ | 72 | 0.4% |

Source: FMCSA Company Census (az4n-8mr2) power units. This band query totals 19,355 carriers; read it as the shape of the distribution.
The fleet-size query totals 19,355 carriers, so read it as the shape of the distribution rather than an exact headcount. Amazon itself has no fleet size requirement for Relay, per its [truck requirements page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-truck-requirements). For what Relay does require, see [Amazon Relay requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## What equipment hauls Amazon freight?

Mostly tractor-trailers. On Amazon-shipper inspections with a weight recorded, 87.7% of vehicles were over 54,000 lb (tractor-trailer class), versus 73.4% on all other 2025+ inspections. In the FMCSA census, 43.1% of carriers with Amazon inspections since 2025 report power only (tractors, no trailers), which fits Amazon's statement that most Relay loads are power only.

This chart shows the equipment carriers report owning in the FMCSA census.
Equipment that carriers hauling Amazon freight report owning:

| Equipment on file | Share of carriers |
|---|---|
| Tractors, no trailers (power only) | 43.1% |
| Tractors and trailers | 30.3% |
| Box or straight trucks only | 14.6% |
| Other or none listed | 12.0% |

Source: FMCSA Company Census (az4n-8mr2) equipment counts for 16,943 carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01.
Of 16,943 carriers in that census group: power only 43.1%, tractors and trailers 30.3%, box or straight trucks only 14.6%, other or none listed 12.0%. More on hauling Amazon's trailers on our [Amazon Relay power only](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/) page.

This chart shows vehicle weight class on Amazon-shipper inspections compared with all other inspections.
Vehicle weight class on Amazon-shipper inspections vs all other inspections:

| Gross combination weight | Amazon-shipper inspections | All other inspections, 2025+ |
|---|---|---|
| Over 54,000 lb (tractor-trailer) | 87.7% | 73.4% |
| 33,001-54,000 lb | 2.5% | 8.7% |
| 19,501-26,000 lb (box truck) | 7.4% | 9.0% |
| 14,001-19,500 lb (step van) | 0.7% | 2.4% |
| 10,001-14,000 lb (large van) | 0.1% | 1.1% |
| 10,000 lb or less | 0.0% | 0.1% |

Source: FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File (fx4q-ay7w), gross_comb_veh_wt, populated on 100,499 of 101,444 Amazon-shipper inspections.
Box truck class vehicles (19,501-26,000 lb) made up 7.4% of Amazon-shipper inspection rows, against 9.0% on other 2025+ inspections. At the carrier level, 83.9% of carriers inspected with Amazon freight since 2025-01-01 ran tractor-trailers and 13.3% ran box trucks. See [Amazon Relay box truck loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck-loads/) for that side of the board.

On the 55,756 units from 2026 Amazon-shipper inspections, 47.9% were truck tractors and 45.9% semi-trailers, with straight trucks at 4.8%. The top tractor makes were Freightliner (15,957), Volvo (6,448) and Kenworth (1,302). The top trailer makes were Hyundai Translead (12,738), Great Dane (3,866), Stoughton (1,922) and Wabash (1,283).

## Do carriers keep hauling Amazon freight?

Recent and frequent Amazon carriers mostly keep hauling it. Of carriers last inspected with Amazon freight 0-3 months before 2026-03-22 and inspected again in the next six months, 64.5% were carrying Amazon freight again. For carriers last seen 27-30 months earlier, that dropped to 15.2%. History matters too: 66.5% with 10+ prior Amazon inspections, 24.7% with one.

This chart shows the share of carriers seen again with Amazon freight, by how recently and how often they were seen before.
Share of carriers caught with Amazon freight again in the next six months, by how recently they were last seen with it:

| Last Amazon-shipper inspection before 2026-03-22 | Again carrying Amazon freight by 2026-09-22 |
|---|---|
| 0-3 months before | 64.5% |
| 3-9 months | 39.4% |
| 9-15 months | 23.9% |
| 15-21 months | 21.4% |
| 21-27 months | 19.0% |
| 27-30 months | 15.2% |

Source: FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File (fx4q-ay7w). Only carriers that were inspected at all between 2026-03-22 and 2026-09-22.
This measures carriers who were inspected again in the six months after 2026-03-22. A carrier that stopped being inspected at all is not counted either way.

## How was this data collected?

We used the FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File, a public dataset updated daily, plus FMCSA's Inspections Per Unit file and Company Census. We counted inspections whose shipper name contains "AMAZON" and the distinct USDOT numbers behind them. The public file covers 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22. We publish aggregates only, with no carrier names or DOT numbers.

**Sources** (queried 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25):

- FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File, dataset fx4q-ay7w: [data.transportation.gov/d/fx4q-ay7w](https://data.transportation.gov/d/fx4q-ay7w)
- FMCSA Inspections Per Unit, dataset wt8s-2hbx: [data.transportation.gov/d/wt8s-2hbx](https://data.transportation.gov/d/wt8s-2hbx)
- FMCSA Company Census, dataset az4n-8mr2: [data.transportation.gov/d/az4n-8mr2](https://data.transportation.gov/d/az4n-8mr2)

**How it works.** When an officer does a roadside inspection, the report records the shipper named on the bill of lading. The public file is a rolling three-year window. FMCSA removes driver information from public inspection files.

**Caveats:**

- **An inspection is not a load.** Most loads are never inspected, so these counts are a floor, not a total.
- **Amazon freight is not the same as Amazon Relay.** Amazon on the bill of lading means Amazon freight, which is not proof the load was booked through Relay. It includes Amazon's own fleets and contract carriers.
- **Shipper name is often blank.** It is filled in on 67.0% of all inspection records (8,314,133 records in the file on 2026-09-24). In 2026, capture by inspection level was 73% for Level 2, 68% for Level 1, 68% for Level 3 and 8% for Level 5 (vehicle only).
- **Spelling varies.** Officers spell Amazon 1,064 different ways in the file. Plain "AMAZON" is the most common.

Download the aggregate numbers as a CSV.
CSV download: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/amazon-relay-carrier-data-2026.csv
## How should you cite this data?

Cite this analysis as NudoIQ analysis of FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File data, naming the inspection date range and the publication date, and link to this page. Note that counts are a floor based on roadside inspections and reflect Amazon freight in general, not only Amazon Relay loads. A suggested citation line follows.

> NudoIQ analysis of FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File data, inspections 2023-09-24 to 2026-09-22, published 2026-10-02.

## What does this mean for carriers on Amazon Relay?

Thousands of carriers haul Amazon freight, and about 530 new ones show up each month, most running 1-5 trucks. On the Relay board that means many small carriers watching the same loads. Speed of booking and knowing what a lane usually pays matter more as more carriers compete for the same freight.

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension for the Amazon Relay load board. It refreshes the board with adjustable timing, alerts you or books when a load matches your rules, and shows each lane's rate history and the net profit on every load card. It doesn't guarantee loads or rates. For the basics of finding work, see [Amazon Relay loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-loads/) and [how much Amazon Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

It's $49.99 a month ([pricing](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing)) with a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start, and you can cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many trucking companies haul for Amazon?
At least 22,866 carriers (USDOT numbers) appeared on FMCSA roadside inspections listing Amazon as the shipper between 2023-09-24 and 2026-09-22. About 16,978 did from 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-22. Because most loads are never inspected, the real number is higher.

### How many carriers are on Amazon Relay?
This analysis can't give a Relay-only count. Public FMCSA inspection data shows carriers hauling Amazon freight in general, which includes Relay carriers, Amazon's own fleets and contract carriers, and it can't separate Relay loads from other Amazon freight.

### Which state has the most Amazon carriers?
California, with 3,011 carriers that had an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01, by physical address. Ohio (1,689) and Illinois (1,589) are next, both ahead of Texas (972).

### Are most Amazon carriers owner-operators?
Most are small. About 70% of carriers with an Amazon-shipper inspection since 2025-01-01 run 1-5 power units, and 9,941 run just 1-2.

### Is this data updated?
The FMCSA Vehicle Inspection File is updated daily and covers a rolling three-year window. The figures on this page come from queries run on 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25 and cover inspections through 2026-09-22.
