# Amazon Relay box truck loads: how to find and book them

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck-loads/
Published: 2026-10-02. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: Amazon Relay has box truck loads for 16 ft and 26 ft dock-height box trucks with a working tuck-under liftgate. Carriers find them by filtering the Relay load board by equipment type, posting the truck with Post A Truck, or booking box truck contracts, including 8-hour and 13-hour solo contracts with round trips.

## What box truck loads does Amazon Relay have?

Amazon Relay has work for 16 ft and 26 ft box trucks that are dock height and have a working tuck-under liftgate. Box trucks can book one-way loads, spot loads from the board and short-term contracts, including 8-hour and 13-hour solo contracts with round trips. Cargo vans can't be used.

That's from [Amazon's truck requirements page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-truck-requirements). To check your truck, insurance and authority first, see our [box truck requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck/).

- **One-way loads.** [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-work-amazon-relay) one-way loads need a box truck or your own trailer, an edge over a tractor with no trailer.
- **Spot freight.** Last-minute loads you book right away.
- **Contracts.** Full or partial weeks of loads booked ahead. A 13-hour solo contract is one day of loads with 11 hours of drive time.
- **Post A Truck.** You post when and where the truck is free, and Amazon matches loads to it.

If you're looking for a 26 ft box truck load board for Amazon freight, the Relay board is it. Amazon tenders its loads only through Relay, not on third-party boards.

## How do you filter the Relay load board for box truck loads?

Open the Relay load board and set the equipment type filter to the box truck size you run. Then narrow by origin or radius, load type, driver type, trip length and pickup window, and save the search. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) the board is open 24/7 and free to search and book.

A setup that works for most box truck carriers:

1. **Equipment type:** your box truck size only, so you don't scroll past loads you can't run.
2. **Origin and radius:** where the truck sits and how far you'll drive empty.
3. **Load type and driver type:** one-way, round trip or both; solo unless you run a team.
4. **Max stops and trip length:** what one shift can handle.
5. **Rate range and time windows:** cut what you'd never book.
6. **Save the search** so it's there every time.

The board also suggests return trips and reloads after you book. If it looks empty, work through our [load board not showing loads checklist](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board-not-showing-loads/). The [Amazon Relay load board guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) covers the rest.

## How do you set up Post A Truck for a box truck?

Post A Truck lets you post your box truck's availability with a minimum rate per mile, and Amazon matches loads to it. Amazon lists box trucks as eligible, along with power only and live loads. Carriers who get matched see that freight first, before it ever reaches the load board.

From [Amazon's Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck), here's what you set:

- **Window:** post the truck and driver up to two weeks ahead.
- **Direction:** one-way or round trip.
- **Cities:** include the ones you want, exclude the ones you don't.
- **Limits:** a cap on distance or duration.
- **Price:** a [minimum rate per mile](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/3-ways-to-set-your-own-freight-rates-on-amazon-relay).

Before you post, read the **Match outlook**: High, Medium or Low odds based on the previous six weeks of loads. If it's Low, widen the cities or the hours.

A block order (same start and end) pays in full even if Amazon doesn't use the whole block. Amazon books loads that match your criteria, so only post a window you can run.

## Should a box truck run Relay contracts or spot loads?

Spot loads are last-minute loads you book on the board right away. Contracts are full or partial weeks of loads booked ahead. Contract access depends on your grade: [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) new contracts need a B or better, and a grade needs ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks.

| | Spot loads | Contracts | Auctions |
|---|---|---|---|
| When you book | Right away, on the board | In advance, for full or partial weeks | Bid ahead on contracts up to 6 months |
| Who sets the price | Amazon lists it, you book at that price | Amazon | You bid; a winning rate is locked for the contract |
| Grade needed | Any grade gets board access | B or above for new contracts | Most bids need C+ or better |

Keep an eye on the floor: Amazon says carriers can lose booked contracts if they drop below C+. A+ and A carriers also get contract price alerts. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains how the grade is built.

## How common are box trucks on Amazon freight?

Box trucks are a real but small share of Amazon freight. In our count of FMCSA roadside inspections that list Amazon as the shipper, the box truck weight class (19,501 to 26,000 lb) is 7.4% of inspection rows. At the carrier level, 13.3% of those carriers were inspected in a box truck.

More from the same public FMCSA data, which we break down on our [Amazon Relay carrier data page](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/):

- **14.6%** of carriers with Amazon-shipper inspections since 2025 list only box or straight trucks in the FMCSA census.
- Straight trucks were **4.8%** of units on 2026 Amazon-shipper inspections. The top makes were Freightliner, International and Hino.

Two caveats. An inspection isn't a load: most loads are never inspected, so these counts are a floor, not a total. And Amazon on the bill of lading means Amazon freight, not proof the load was booked through Relay; it includes Amazon's own fleets and contract carriers.

## How do you tell if a box truck rate is good?

Start with what the price includes. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) a Relay rate shows a base rate, a fuel surcharge that tracks fuel prices, and tolls. Then take out your own costs and the empty miles to pickup. Distance, trip direction, equipment, live loads, season and region all move the rate.

Ask on every load:

- **How far is the deadhead?** You pay for the empty miles to pickup.
- **Which way does it leave you?** A one-way that ends near home beats one that strands the truck two hours out.
- **Is it a live load?** Check the details so the wait doesn't eat the shift.
- **What's left after costs?** Fuel, maintenance and driver pay come out first.

Pay varies by lane, timing and equipment, and Amazon doesn't publish typical box truck rates. More on that in [how much Amazon Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

## Why do box truck loads disappear so fast?

Good loads on the Relay board get booked within seconds because a lot of carriers watch the same filters. Amazon also shows new spot loads to A+, A and B+ carriers first, at staggered times. By the time you reload by hand, a clean round trip near you can already be gone.

What helps:

- **Amazon's own alerts.** Saved searches, email alerts and mobile push notifications.
- **A refresher.** It reloads the board every few seconds for you. See [how Amazon Relay auto refresh works](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/).
- **Rules and auto-booking.** An auto-booker books only loads that match your lane, price and limits. See our [auto-booker guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/).
- **Protecting acceptance.** Cancelling a booked load hurts your acceptance score, more the closer it is to pickup. Book only what the truck can run.

## Where does NudoIQ fit for a box truck carrier?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It refreshes the board on a 1 to 5 second interval with jitter, alerts you on matching loads, and can book them by your rules. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon.

- **Alert, Search and Autobook modes** with lane and price rules. Autobook stops at your max-books cap and won't book under your profit floor. Telegram alerts tell you when a load lands.
- **Net profit on every load card**: the rate minus driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead to pickup.
- **Lane Intelligence**: the posted price next to that lane's 90-day history. It's decision support, not a guarantee.
- **Post A Truck helper**: board price next to your minimum $/mile and payout, then post with one button.
- **Backhaul finder**: loads from where your current load ends, pointed back toward home.

It's [$49.99 a month](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing) for every feature, the same price for one truck or twenty. Start with a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you use a cargo van for Amazon Relay loads?
No. Amazon says cargo vans can't be used on Relay. Its box truck options are 16 ft and 26 ft trucks with a working tuck-under liftgate.

### Do I need a liftgate for Amazon box truck loads?
Yes. Amazon requires a working tuck-under liftgate on both 16 ft and 26 ft box trucks. A box truck without one doesn't meet the equipment rules.

### Is there a minimum fleet size to haul box truck loads for Amazon?
No. Amazon says there's no fleet size requirement to haul for Relay, so a single box truck can qualify. Your authority, insurance and safety record still have to meet the [Amazon Relay requirements](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

### Are Amazon box truck loads posted on DAT or other load boards?
No. Amazon tenders its loads only through the Relay load board, not on third-party boards. You need an approved Relay carrier account to see and book them.

### How fast does Amazon pay for box truck loads?
Amazon pays weekly on a Sunday to Saturday cycle. Loads finished before 11:59 pm Saturday are paid the following Friday, and invoices are created automatically, per the [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq).

# Amazon Relay power only: how it works and how to book it

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/
Published: 2026-10-02. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: Power only on Amazon Relay means the carrier brings the tractor and Amazon provides the trailer. Amazon says the majority of Relay loads are power only, and round trips usually need only a tractor. Day cab and sleeper tractors both qualify. One-way loads need your own trailer or a box truck.

## What does power only mean on Amazon Relay?

Power only means you bring the tractor and Amazon provides the trailer. In [Amazon's words](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-truck-requirements), the majority of Relay loads are power only. You hook to an Amazon-owned trailer and haul it. Amazon says this cuts facility wait time and trailer maintenance costs for carriers.

What it means day to day:

- **No trailer to buy for most Relay work.** A day cab or sleeper tractor is enough for power only loads.
- **You're pulling Amazon's equipment.** Amazon's insurance rules include $50,000 of trailer interchange coverage for semi operators. See our [insurance requirements page](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/).
- **You still need an approved carrier account.** Our [Amazon Relay requirements checklist](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/) covers authority, safety and equipment.

## Which Amazon Relay loads are power only?

[Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-work-amazon-relay) round trips, which start and end at the same domicile, usually need only a tractor. That makes round trips the core of power only work. One-way loads are different: Amazon says they need a box truck or your own trailer, so a tractor alone won't cover them.

How the main work types line up for a tractor with no trailer:

| Work type | What it is | Power only fit |
|---|---|---|
| Round trip | Starts and ends at the same domicile | Usually tractor only |
| One-way | Head haul or backhaul to cut deadhead | Needs your own trailer (or a box truck) |
| Block | A chunk of time you reserve trucks and drivers for | Paid even if Amazon doesn't use the full block |
| Spot freight | Last-minute loads booked right away on the board | Filter by equipment and trailer status |
| Contract | Full or partial weeks of loads, booked ahead | Needs a B grade or better for new contracts |

On the [Relay load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/), use the equipment type and trailer status filters so you only see loads your tractor can take.

## Should you run a day cab or a sleeper on Relay power only?

Both qualify. Relay supports day cab and sleeper tractors, and the right one depends on how long your driver stays out. Amazon describes three setups: 13-hour solo (one day of loads, 11 hours of drive time), 37-hour solo (two days, with the 10-hour break taken outside base cities) and team.

- **13-hour solo:** one day of loads. If you run a day cab, start here.
- **37-hour solo:** the 10-hour break happens away from base cities, so plan where your driver sleeps before you book.
- **Team:** two drivers trade off.

Amazon doesn't say which cab type each setup requires, so check the load details. Federal [Hours of Service rules](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/regulations/hours-service/summary-hours-service-regulations) (11 hours of driving inside a 14-hour window after 10 hours off) apply either way.

## How do you get power only contracts and auctions on Relay?

Your performance grade decides it. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) carriers need a B or better to book new contracts and C+ or better for most freight auctions. You earn a grade after ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks, so new carriers start on the spot board.

- **Any grade:** load board access, Relay Rewards eligibility and Post A Truck.
- **C+ and up:** freight auctions on high-demand routes. [Auctions](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/3-ways-to-set-your-own-freight-rates-on-amazon-relay) cover contracts up to 6 months, you bid in bulk by spreadsheet, and the winning rate is locked for the contract. Eligibility also depends on equipment count, tenure and CARB compliance.
- **B and up:** new contracts. A+ and A carriers also get contract price alerts.
- **A+, A and B+:** early access to new spot loads, which show up at staggered times by grade.

Drop below C+ and you can lose contracts you already booked. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains the four metrics behind the grade.

## How does Post A Truck work for power only?

Post A Truck lets you post your tractor's availability and a minimum rate per mile, and Amazon matches loads to it. Amazon lists power only as eligible. You can post up to two weeks ahead, choose one-way or round trip, include or exclude cities, and set distance or duration limits.

From [Amazon's Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck):

- **Match outlook** shows High, Medium or Low odds from the previous six weeks of loads.
- **Matched carriers get first access** to freight in their window before it reaches the load board.
- **Block orders** (same start and end) pay in full even if Amazon doesn't use the whole block.
- **Higher grades get priority matching.**

Amazon books loads that match your criteria, so post only the hours your driver can actually run.

## What does FMCSA data show about Amazon power only carriers?

Tractor-trailers carry almost all inspected Amazon freight. In our count of FMCSA roadside inspections that list Amazon as the shipper, 87.7% of rows are in the over 54,000 lb tractor-trailer class. And 43.1% of carriers hauling Amazon freight list tractors but no trailers in the FMCSA census.

More from the same public data, broken down on our [Amazon Relay carrier data page](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-carrier-data/):

- **Compared with everyone else:** the tractor-trailer class is 73.4% of all other 2025+ inspections.
- **What carriers own:** power only (tractors, no trailers) 43.1%; tractors and trailers 30.3%; box or straight trucks only 14.6%; other or none listed 12.0%.
- **Trailers on 2026 inspections:** Hyundai Translead (12,738), Great Dane (3,866), Stoughton (1,922), Wabash (1,283).
- **Tractors on 2026 inspections:** Freightliner (15,957), Volvo (6,448), Kenworth (1,302).

Two caveats. An inspection isn't a load: most loads are never inspected, so these counts are a floor. And Amazon on the bill of lading means Amazon freight, not proof the load was booked through Relay; it includes Amazon's own fleets and contract carriers.

## How do you judge a power only rate on Relay?

Read what the price includes, then what it costs you to run. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) a Relay rate is a base rate, a fuel surcharge that tracks fuel prices, and tolls. Distance (including deadhead and trip direction), equipment, live loads, season and regional demand all move it.

Check these before you book:

- **Deadhead to the hook.** Empty miles to pick up the trailer cost you fuel and hours.
- **Trip direction.** A round trip brings the tractor home. A load heading away from base can leave you hunting for the next one.
- **Live loads.** Check trailer status and the load details so you know what you're signing up for.
- **Net after costs.** Driver pay, fuel and maintenance come out first.

Pay varies by lane, timing and equipment, and Amazon doesn't publish typical rates. More in [how much Amazon Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

## When does owning a trailer help on Amazon Relay?

A trailer opens one-way loads. Amazon says one-way loads need a box truck or your own trailer, and one-ways are how you book head hauls and backhauls to cut deadhead. Without a trailer, you're working round trips, blocks and the power only loads on the board.

Relay supports 48 ft and 53 ft dry vans. A 53 ft reefer must meet the FDA Sanitary Transportation Rule, and 20, 40 or 45 ft high cube containers need UIIA. Before buying, count how many one-ways near your base you pass on today.

## Where does NudoIQ help a power only carrier?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It refreshes the board on a 1 to 5 second interval with jitter, alerts you on matching power only loads, and can book them by your rules. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon.

- **Alert, Search and Autobook modes** with lane and price rules. Autobook stops at your max-books cap and won't book under your profit floor. See our [auto-booker guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/).
- **Net profit on every load card:** the rate minus driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead to pickup.
- **Lane Intelligence:** the posted price next to that lane's 90-day history. It's decision support, not a guarantee.
- **Post A Truck helper** and a **backhaul finder** that searches from where your load ends back toward home.

It's [$49.99 a month](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing) for every feature, the same price for one truck or twenty. Start with a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need my own trailer for Amazon Relay?
Not for most loads. Amazon says the majority of Relay loads are power only and round trips usually need only a tractor. You need your own trailer (or a box truck) for one-way loads.

### What insurance do I need to pull Amazon trailers?
Amazon requires $1,000,000 auto liability per occurrence and $50,000 trailer interchange for semi operators, along with cargo and general liability. The [Relay insurance guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-insurance-requirements) lists every coverage.

### Is there a minimum number of trucks for Amazon Relay power only?
No. Amazon says there's no fleet size requirement to haul for Relay. A single tractor can qualify if your authority, insurance and safety record meet the rules.

### Are Amazon power only loads posted on other load boards?
No. Amazon tenders its loads only through the Relay load board, not on third-party boards. You need an approved Relay carrier account to book them.

# Amazon Relay dispatcher: what the job is and how to do it well

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-dispatcher/
Published: 2026-10-02. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: An Amazon Relay dispatcher searches and books loads on the carrier's Relay account, assigns them to invited drivers, watches live load tracking and handles problems in transit. The carrier stays responsible for its account and performance score. Carriers can dispatch in-house, hire a dispatch service, or use tools that alert and book by rules.

## What does an Amazon Relay dispatcher do?

A Relay dispatcher finds and books loads on the carrier's account, puts each load on a driver, and watches it through delivery. When something goes wrong in transit, the dispatcher handles it, and when the score takes a hit, the dispatcher files the dispute. The job is booking, assigning, tracking and protecting the score.

The day usually looks like this:

- **Search and book.** Work the [Relay load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/), saved searches and Post A Truck to keep every truck covered.
- **Assign drivers.** [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/driver-eligibility-requirements-to-haul-amazon-loads) carriers manage their drivers and decide which ones get Amazon loads.
- **Watch the trip.** Follow live tracking and step in when a load stalls.
- **Handle disruptions and disputes.** Carriers can dispute performance score impacts when something happens in transit. Amazon decides every dispute.
- **Keep the paperwork straight.** The carrier stays responsible for drug and alcohol testing, Hours of Service and medical certification.

If you're searching "box truck dispatch" or "dispatchers for box trucks", the same job applies. Box trucks and tractors book on the same board, through the same account. See our guides to [Amazon Relay box truck loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck-loads/) and [Relay power only](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/).

## How do drivers get set up under a Relay carrier?

Drivers can only create a Relay profile by invitation from a Relay-approved carrier, and there are no shared accounts. Amazon verifies each driver with the front and back of their CDL plus a selfie, usually within 48 hours, and runs background checks. Drivers then use the Relay app on iOS or Android.

What a dispatcher needs to stay on top of:

1. **Send the invite** from the carrier account. Each driver gets their own profile.
2. **Get verification done early.** The CDL and selfie review is typically done within 48 hours, so don't promise a driver a load before they clear it.
3. **Expect selfies on the road.** The app asks for periodic selfies during loads, for example at pickup or drop-off.
4. **Keep the app open with location on.** Amazon's app usage metric checks that drivers keep the Relay app running and location services on for the whole trip.

That last one matters more than most dispatchers think. App usage is one of the four metrics in the [Amazon Relay performance score](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score), and a driver who closes the app can pull the whole score down.

## What can a dispatcher see in Relay load tracking?

Relay's load tracking shows owner-operators, fleet managers and dispatchers each trip in real time, updated about every 30 seconds. It includes disruption signals, a route view, weather, trip playback, and the driver's contact details and status. It only works while the driver keeps the app open with location services on.

From [Amazon's load tracking page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/load-tracking-with-amazon-relay), here's what that gives you:

| Tracking feature | What a dispatcher uses it for |
|---|---|
| Live position, about every 30 seconds | Seeing if a driver will make the check-in time |
| Disruption signals | Catching a stalled trailer before it becomes a score hit |
| Route view and weather | Planning around delays on the way |
| Trip playback | Backing up a dispute with what actually happened |
| Driver contact and status | Reaching the driver fast when plans change |

## Should you hire a dispatch service or dispatch yourself?

It depends on your time and your margins. Dispatch services commonly charge either a percentage of each load or a flat fee, so compare that with what it costs to do it in-house. Either way, the carrier stays responsible for its Relay account, its drivers and its performance score.

| | Dispatch yourself | Hire a dispatch service | Dispatch with tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who books | You or your office | The service | You, with alerts or rules-based booking |
| Cost | Your time | A percentage of each load or a flat fee | A software subscription |
| Who answers for the score | The carrier | Still the carrier | The carrier |
| What to watch | Burnout from watching the board | What they book in your name | Rules set too loose |

Two things to check before you bring in a service:

- **Amazon doesn't publish rules about outside dispatch services.** Read Relay's terms yourself before you bring one in. Nothing here says Amazon allows or bans them.
- **Every booking is yours.** If a dispatcher books a load a driver can't make and it gets cancelled close to pickup, the acceptance penalty lands on your account.

## How does a dispatcher protect the Relay performance score?

Book only what your drivers can run, get them there on time, and keep the app on. Amazon scores four metrics (on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free), and your overall score is the lowest of the four. One weak metric sets the grade, and the grade decides access to contracts and early loads.

Per [Amazon's grade guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) and the score page:

- **Acceptance.** Cancelling a booked load counts against you, including loads that expire. The closer to pickup you cancel, the bigger the penalty. Decide early.
- **On-time.** Loads have to arrive by the planned time at origin and destination, measured from the check-in timestamp. Build slack for traffic and Hours of Service.
- **App usage.** Drivers keep the Relay app running with location on for the whole trip.
- **Disruption-free.** Stationary trailers and loads with no assigned driver count against you. Assign every load to a driver.

The score covers your last six weeks of hauls, and Amazon gives a daily prediction of your upcoming score in the account. Check it every morning. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) goes deeper on grades and disputes.

## What load boards do Relay dispatchers use?

For Amazon freight, the only board is the Relay load board. Amazon tenders its loads only through Relay, not on third-party boards. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) it's open 24/7 and free to search and book, with filters, saved searches, email alerts and mobile push notifications for a dispatcher working several trucks.

Useful board features for dispatchers:

- **Filters** for origin, destination or radius, equipment type, trailer status, load type, driver type, max stops, trip length, rate range and pickup and delivery windows.
- **Saved searches**, one per truck or lane.
- **Reload and return-trip suggestions** to keep a driver moving after the first load.
- **Post A Truck** to post availability up to two weeks ahead with a minimum rate per mile.

Good loads still get booked within seconds, which is why many dispatchers add a [refresher](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/) or an [auto-booker](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/).

## Where does NudoIQ help a Relay dispatcher?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It watches the board for you, alerts you on loads that match your rules, and can book them with a cap and a profit floor. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon.

What a dispatcher gets:

- **Alert, Search and Autobook modes** with lane and price rules. Autobook stops at your max-books cap (set it to the trucks you can cover) and won't book under your profit floor.
- **Telegram alerts** when a load lands, so you're not tied to the screen.
- **Lane Intelligence:** the posted price next to that lane's 90-day history. It's decision support, not a guarantee.
- **Net profit on every load card:** the rate minus driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead to pickup.
- **Driver dispatch by text or email** when you assign a load, plus an HOS overview.

It's [$49.99 a month](https://nudoiq.com/#pricing) for every feature, the same price for one truck or twenty. Start with a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start, and cancel anytime. NudoIQ is rated 5.0 on the Chrome Web Store.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Amazon allow third-party dispatchers on Relay?
Amazon doesn't publish rules about outside dispatch services. The carrier is responsible for its Relay account, so read Relay's terms before you bring in a service.

### How much does a box truck dispatcher charge?
Dispatch services commonly charge either a percentage of each load or a flat fee. Prices vary by service, so get it in writing and compare it with the cost of dispatching in-house.

### Can drivers share one Amazon Relay account?
No. Each driver needs their own Relay profile, created by invitation from the carrier, and Amazon doesn't allow shared accounts.

### How long does Amazon Relay driver verification take?
Amazon says the CDL and selfie review is typically done within 48 hours. Background checks are also required before a driver hauls.

### Who is responsible for Hours of Service on Amazon Relay loads?
The carrier. Amazon says carriers stay responsible for Hours of Service, drug and alcohol testing and medical certification. Federal rules allow [11 hours of driving within a 14-hour window](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/regulations/hours-service/summary-hours-service-regulations) after 10 hours off.

# Amazon Relay account suspended or can't book loads? What to check

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-account-suspended/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: Amazon doesn't publish suspension rules, appeal steps or reinstatement timelines. What it does publish: an insurance lapse blocks booking and hauling until coverage is reinstated, and Amazon monitors carrier compliance through internal teams and a third-party service. Check your Insurance tab and authority first, then contact the Support Center from your Relay account.

## Why can't I book loads on Amazon Relay?

The most common reason Amazon itself names is insurance. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-insurance-requirements) that if your coverage lapses, your company can't book or haul Relay loads until it's reinstated.

Beyond that, [Amazon's FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says it uses internal compliance teams and a third-party compliance monitoring service to validate and continually monitor carriers. It doesn't list which problems lead to which action. So start with the things you can check yourself:

- **Insurance:** every policy current in the Insurance tab of your Relay account.
- **Authority:** your DOT and MC numbers active on FMCSA's SAFER site.
- **Messages:** any notice or email from Amazon, and the exact wording you see when you try to book.

If the board just looks empty and you can still book, that's a different problem. See [Relay load board not showing loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board-not-showing-loads/).

## Is my Relay account suspended, or is it something else?

Not every lockout is a suspension. Several published Relay rules limit what you can book without shutting the account:

| What you see | Possible cause Amazon publishes | Where to check |
|---|---|---|
| Can't book or haul any loads | Insurance lapse | Insurance tab in your Relay account |
| Can't book new contracts | Grade below B | Scorecard in the Relay portal |
| Lost contracts you already booked | Grade dropped below C+ | Scorecard |
| Can't join freight auctions | Grade below C+ (reefer auctions need B) | Scorecard |
| New spot loads show up later for you | Early access goes to A+, A and B+ | Scorecard |
| Driver can't use the Relay app | Driver profile not invited or not verified yet | Your driver list and the driver's app |
| Application turned down | Fixable issue or a serious compliance issue | Your application status |

The grade rules come from [Amazon's performance grades guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities). Every grade keeps load board access, so a low grade alone doesn't take the board away. Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains the four metrics.

For drivers, [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/driver-eligibility-requirements-to-haul-amazon-loads) profiles are created only by invitation from an approved carrier, and it reviews the CDL and a selfie, typically within 48 hours.

## What does Amazon check to keep a carrier active?

Amazon publishes its carrier requirements and keeps monitoring compliance after approval. It doesn't say which slip triggers what, so check each requirement.

From the [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq):

- A DOT number with interstate authority, active at least 180 days, and a valid MC number.
- Entity type Carrier, authorized for Property and For-Hire.
- FMCSA safety rating of Satisfactory, None or Not Rated.
- BASIC scores under Amazon's limits: Unsafe Driving and HOS Compliance below 60%; Vehicle Maintenance, Controlled Substances/Alcohol and Driver Fitness below 75%.
- Driver out-of-service rate at or below 35% and vehicle violation rate at or below 50%.
- Verification of the business and every owner with more than 25%.
- Insurance at or above the minimums.

The full list is on our [Amazon Relay requirements checklist](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-requirements/).

## How do I fix an insurance lapse on Relay?

Renew the policy, then get the new details into your Relay account. Amazon tells carriers to renew two to three weeks before expiry so RMIS can update records, and to add updated details in the Insurance tab at least 5 days before the policy expires.

If it already lapsed:

1. Renew or replace the policy with your agent.
2. Make sure your new certificate reaches RMIS.
3. Update the Insurance tab with the new dates.
4. Contact the Support Center and say what you updated.

Amazon's coverage minimums, policy by policy, are on our [insurance requirements page](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/).

## Who do I contact when my Relay account is suspended?

Use the Support Center in your Relay account. Amazon's FAQ sends account-access problems there when you're logged in. For problems with a load in progress, the Relay Operations Center (ROC) offers 24/7 support through the Relay portal or Relay mobile.

Amazon doesn't publish a support phone number, or a separate route if you can't log in at all. Be careful with any number or "reinstatement service" you find elsewhere that isn't on relay.amazon.com.

## Can I appeal an Amazon Relay suspension?

Amazon doesn't publish an appeal process. There are no published steps, deadlines, limits on how many times you can ask, or success rates. The Support Center is the only channel Amazon names for account problems.

Before you write in, have these ready so you can explain it once:

- The exact message or email from Amazon, with the date.
- A screenshot of what you see when you try to book.
- Your current certificate of insurance.
- Your DOT and MC numbers and their status on SAFER.

## How long does an Amazon Relay suspension last?

Amazon doesn't say. It publishes no reinstatement timeline. For insurance, booking stays blocked until coverage is reinstated, so update the Insurance tab fast.

## Can I reapply to Amazon Relay after being rejected or deactivated?

For rejected applications, yes in some cases. The FAQ says you may be eligible to reapply once a fixable issue like insurance coverage, authority status or missing documentation is resolved, and that serious compliance issues may disqualify you.

Amazon doesn't publish a waiting period, and it says nothing about reapplying after an active account is deactivated. Ask the Support Center for your case.

## Can a low scorecard get my Relay account suspended?

Amazon doesn't list the scorecard as a suspension reason. It does tie your grade to what you can book. Your overall score equals your lowest of four metrics (on-time, acceptance, app usage and disruption-free) over the last six weeks. A drop can cost you contracts, auctions and early access to spot loads. You can dispute score impacts from your Relay account, and Amazon decides each one.

## Can a load board extension or dispatcher get my account suspended?

Nobody outside Amazon can honestly answer that. Amazon doesn't publish what triggers a suspension, so no one can promise any tool, dispatcher or setting will or won't affect your account. Your account is your responsibility: read the Relay terms you agreed to, and never hand your Amazon password to anyone.

NudoIQ runs inside your own signed-in Relay tab and never asks for your Amazon password. It makes no promise about account status. New to Relay? Start with [what Amazon Relay is](https://nudoiq.com/what-is-amazon-relay/) and how the [load board](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) works.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a phone number for Amazon Relay support?
Amazon doesn't publish one. Account problems go to the Support Center in your Relay account, and load problems go to the Relay Operations Center through the portal or Relay mobile.

### How long does it take to get reinstated on Amazon Relay?
Amazon doesn't publish a reinstatement timeline. For an insurance lapse, booking stays blocked until coverage is reinstated, so update the Insurance tab as soon as you renew.

### Why does Relay say I can't book loads?
Amazon's published reason is an insurance lapse. It also monitors compliance through internal teams and a third-party service. Check your insurance and authority, then contact the Support Center.

### Can I appeal a Relay deactivation?
Amazon doesn't publish appeal steps, deadlines or success rates. Contact the Support Center with your documents and the exact message you received.

### Can I reapply after my Relay application was rejected?
Possibly. Amazon says you may reapply once a fixable issue like insurance, authority or missing documents is resolved. Serious compliance issues may disqualify you. No waiting period is published.

### Does a low grade block me from the Relay load board?
No. Amazon says every grade keeps load board access. Lower grades lose new contracts (below B), auctions (below C+) and early access to spot loads.

# Amazon Relay load board not showing loads: what to check

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board-not-showing-loads/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: Usually a filter or saved search is set too narrow: equipment type, trailer status, radius, trip length, rate range or time windows. Next, check your account, since lapsed insurance stops booking. Lower grades see new spot loads later. Then test your browser and extensions, and contact the Relay Operations Center if it's still empty.

## Why is my Amazon Relay load board empty?

Most of the time a filter is hiding the loads. The board only shows work that matches your search, so one setting that's too tight can make it look empty even when freight is posted.

[Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) the board is open 24/7, is free to search and book, and carries thousands of loads at any time. It also says the board can "auto-refresh thousands of new spot freight matches every 30 seconds." So a truly blank board, with every filter cleared, is unusual.

Check filters first, then account status, your grade, your browser, and finally support. New to the board? Our [Amazon Relay load board guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) covers the basics.

## Which filters hide loads on the Relay load board?

Any of them can, if it's set narrower than you meant. Amazon lists the filters across [its load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) and [its freight search guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search).

| Filter | What to check |
|---|---|
| Origin and destination | A specific city on either end cuts out everything else. Try origin only. |
| Location radius (distance willing to travel) | A small radius around a quiet area can return nothing. Widen it. |
| Equipment type | It must match what you actually run. |
| Trailer status | Set it to match the loads your truck can take. |
| Load type | Make sure you haven't excluded the work you want. |
| Driver type | Match how you staff the truck. |
| Layout | Check it isn't set tighter than you intend. |
| Maximum number of stops | A low limit drops multi-stop loads. |
| Trip length | A short range hides longer runs, and the other way around. |
| Rate range | A high minimum hides loads priced below it. |
| Pickup and delivery windows | Narrow windows drop loads outside those hours. |

**Saved searches deserve their own check.** Amazon lets you save your most-used searches, and it uses search history and saved searches for personalized load recommendations. An old saved search with tight settings can quietly load every time you open the board.

The quick test: clear every filter, look at the full board, then add filters back one at a time. When the loads disappear, you've found the setting. Our guide to [Amazon Relay loads](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-loads/) explains the load types, and the [power only](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/) and [box truck](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-box-truck-loads/) guides cover equipment settings.

## Can my account status block the Relay load board?

It can stop you from booking. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-insurance-requirements) that if your insurance coverage lapses, your company can't book or haul Relay loads until it's reinstated. Amazon doesn't say whether loads still display during a lapse.

Amazon also says it uses internal compliance teams and a third-party monitoring service to [continually monitor carrier compliance](https://relay.amazon.com/faq). It doesn't publish what a compliance issue does to board access, so don't assume either way.

Check your account:

- Look for any notice in the Relay portal about insurance, authority or compliance, and follow its instructions.
- Open the Insurance tab and confirm your policy dates.
- Amazon says to renew two to three weeks before expiry and add the updated details at least 5 days before the policy expires.

More on coverage in our [insurance requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/). If your account was suspended or deactivated, see [Amazon Relay account suspended](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-account-suspended/). Amazon doesn't publish suspension categories or reinstatement timelines.

## Does my performance grade change which loads I see?

It changes when you see new spot loads, not whether you can use the board. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) every grade gets load board access. Carriers graded A+, A and B+ get early access to new spot loads, which appear on the board at staggered times by grade.

So with a lower grade, some new loads may already be booked by the time they reach you. Amazon doesn't publish how long the delay is for each grade.

Post A Truck matches also come first: Amazon says matched carriers get first access to freight in their window [before it reaches the load board](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck). And you only get a grade after ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks.

Our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explains the four metrics behind your grade.

## Could a browser extension be the problem?

It could. Any extension that changes web pages can interfere with how the board loads, and your browser session can also get stuck. Amazon doesn't publish a list of supported browsers or extensions, so test it yourself:

- Reload the page.
- Sign out of Relay, then sign back in.
- Close the browser fully and reopen it.
- Turn off your extensions one at a time, reloading the board after each, to see if one is the cause.
- Try another Chromium browser, such as Microsoft Edge, or a fresh Chrome profile with no extensions.

If you use NudoIQ, include it in that test. NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs in your own Chrome, inside your signed-in Relay tab, and never asks for your Amazon password. Its refresher reloads the board on an interval you set from 1 to 5 seconds, with up to 20% random jitter, and keeps the tab from going idle. Alert, Search and Autobook modes ping you on a match, highlight it, or book it by your rules. It's $49.99 a month after a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start. Compare options in our [best Amazon Relay extensions guide](https://nudoiq.com/best-amazon-relay-extensions/) and our [auto-refresh guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-refresh/).

## When should I contact Relay support?

Contact support once you've cleared your filters, checked your account and tested your browser, and the board is still empty. [Amazon says](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) it offers 24/7 operational support through the Relay Operations Center (ROC), reached through the Relay portal or Relay mobile. For account access problems, use the Support Center while logged in.

Before you reach out, have ready:

- A screenshot of the empty board with your filters showing.
- What you already tried.
- Any notice your account shows about insurance or compliance.

Amazon doesn't publish a support phone number, so use the portal or the app.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does my Amazon Relay load board show no loads?
Usually a filter or saved search is set too narrow. Clear every filter, then add them back one at a time. If it's still empty, check your insurance status, test your browser with extensions off, and contact the Relay Operations Center.

### Can a saved search make the board look empty?
Yes. Amazon lets you save your most-used searches. If an old one has tight settings, it can hide loads every time you open the board. Clear it or save a new, wider search.

### Does a lapsed insurance policy stop me from booking Relay loads?
Yes. Amazon says that if your coverage lapses, your company can't book or haul Relay loads until it's reinstated. Renew two to three weeks early and update the Insurance tab at least 5 days before expiry.

### Do higher grades see loads first on Amazon Relay?
Yes for new spot loads. Amazon says A+, A and B+ carriers get early access, and loads appear at staggered times by grade. Every grade still has load board access.

### How often does the Relay load board refresh?
Amazon says the board can auto-refresh thousands of new spot freight matches every 30 seconds.

### Are there more loads at certain times of year?
Yes. Amazon says load volume nearly doubles during peak periods such as Prime Day and the holidays.

### How do I contact Amazon Relay support about the load board?
Use the Relay Operations Center through the Relay portal or Relay mobile. It's available 24/7. For account access problems, use the Support Center while logged in. Amazon doesn't publish a phone number.

# How to book multiple loads on Amazon Relay

URL: https://nudoiq.com/how-to-book-multiple-loads-on-amazon-relay/
Published: 2026-09-20. Last updated: 2026-10-02.

Short answer: To book multiple loads on Amazon Relay, book the first load, then use the load board's reload and return-trip suggestions, or post your truck with Post A Truck up to two weeks ahead. Blocks and contracts reserve more work at once. Before each extra load, check the pickup window, deadhead and your remaining Hours of Service.

## How do you book back-to-back loads on Amazon Relay?

One at a time: book the first load, then find a second that picks up near the first delivery, inside the hours your driver has left. Amazon's [load board guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) doesn't describe a way to book several spot loads in one action.

What helps you chain them on the board:

- **Filters.** Origin and destination (or a radius), equipment type, trailer status, load type, driver type, maximum stops, trip length, rate range, and pickup and delivery windows.
- **Saved searches and alerts.** Save the search you run from your usual delivery points. Relay also has email alerts and push notifications.
- **All-in prices.** The spot price includes the base rate, fuel surcharge and tolls, and you book at the listed price.

More on filters and timing in our [Amazon Relay load board guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/).

## How do reload and return-trip suggestions work?

After you book, the board can suggest more loads for the same truck. Amazon says it suggests replacements for cancelled loads, return trips, and additional loads to continue a driver's journey.

They're suggestions, not bookings. Before you take one, check:

- **Pickup window.** Can your driver get there after the first delivery?
- **Deadhead.** How far is the empty run from the first drop to the next pickup?
- **Hours.** Does the driver have the drive time left (next section)?

Amazon also says [personalized load recommendations](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search) come from your search history and saved searches.

## How do you fit a second load inside Hours of Service?

Add up the first load, the deadhead and the second load, then compare the total to the hours your driver has left. Under [FMCSA Hours of Service rules](https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/regulations/hours-service/summary-hours-service-regulations), a property-carrying driver can drive 11 hours within a 14-hour window after 10 consecutive hours off duty.

A checklist before you book load two:

1. Driving time for load one, start to final stop.
2. Deadhead driving from the last drop to the next pickup.
3. Driving time for load two.
4. Total driving under 11 hours? If not, it doesn't fit today.
5. Does everything, including waits at the docks, finish inside the 14-hour window?
6. Can the driver make the pickup window, not just the last minute of it?

Example with made-up numbers: 4 hours of driving, a 1 hour deadhead and 5 more hours is 10 hours, under 11. If dock time pushes the day past 14 hours, it still doesn't fit.

[Some spot loads offer pickup time options](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-use-amazon-relays-load-board) at booking to allow for traffic, stem miles and Hours of Service. Not all do. Amazon also describes [three driver setups](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trucking-work-amazon-relay):

| Setup | What Amazon says |
|---|---|
| 13-hour solo | One day of loads, including 11 hours of drive time |
| 37-hour solo | Two days of loads, with the 10-hour break taken outside base cities |
| Team | Two drivers trade off |

## Can Post A Truck line up your next load?

Yes. Post A Truck lets you post when and where your truck is free, and Amazon books loads that match. [Amazon's Post A Truck guide](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/how-to-load-match-with-post-a-truck) says you can post up to two weeks ahead, include or exclude cities, pick one-way or round trip, and set distance or duration limits. You set a minimum rate per mile.

Why it helps with a second load:

- **Match outlook** shows High, Medium or Low odds, based on the previous six weeks of loads.
- **First access.** Matched carriers see freight in their window before it reaches the load board.
- **Block orders** with the same start and end pay in full even if Amazon doesn't use the whole block.

Amazon says it will [instantly book loads that match your criteria](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-to-find-truck-loads-faster-with-amazon-relays-free-freight-search), so only post hours your driver can actually run. A post isn't a guaranteed match. Amazon doesn't publish how many posts you can have open at once.

## Do blocks or contracts beat chaining spot loads?

They reserve more work up front, so you're not hunting for each next load. Whether they beat spot depends on your lanes, your grade and what the rates are that week.

| Option | How it works | Who can book |
|---|---|---|
| Spot loads | Last-minute loads booked one at a time | All grades |
| Block | A chunk of time you reserve trucks and drivers for, paid even if Amazon doesn't use the full block | Not listed on Amazon's grades page |
| Contract | Full or partial weeks of loads, booked in advance | B grade or better for new contracts |
| Auction | Contracts up to 6 months, bid in bulk, winning rate locked | C+ or better for most bids |

Amazon's [grades page](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/relay-performance-grades-how-to-unlock-hauling-opportunities) says carriers can lose booked contracts if they drop below C+. You get a grade after ten or more Relay loads in the last six active weeks, so new carriers start on spot. See Amazon's [rate options](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/3-ways-to-set-your-own-freight-rates-on-amazon-relay) for auctions, and our guide to [what Relay pays](https://nudoiq.com/how-much-does-amazon-relay-pay/).

## What happens if you book too many and cancel?

It hurts your score. [Amazon's performance score](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-performance-score) includes an acceptance metric that tracks how often you reject (cancel) loads you booked, including expired loads. The closer the cancellation is to pickup, the bigger the penalty.

Why it matters:

- **Your overall score is your lowest metric.** One weak metric sets your grade.
- **Grades unlock work.** B for new contracts, C+ for most auctions, and A+, A and B+ for early access to new spot loads.
- **Amazon doesn't publish** the penalty size for a cancellation, the score cutoff for each grade, or how long a single cancellation stays on your score.

The simple habit: don't book load two until you've done the hours math. More in our [scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/).

## Can a tool book multiple loads for you?

Yes. Amazon's Post A Truck books matching loads for you, and third-party browser extensions exist. Whatever you use, you're responsible for your Relay account, so check Relay's terms.

Ask any auto-booker:

- **Does it stop at a cap** on how many loads it books?
- **Does it respect a profit floor** you set?
- **Do you set the lanes and prices?**

Our [Amazon Relay auto-booker guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auto-booker/) goes deeper.

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is a Chrome extension that runs inside your signed-in Relay load board tab. It's an independent tool, not made by or affiliated with Amazon. Autobook books loads that match the price and lane rules you set, and stops at your max-books cap and your profit floor. A backhaul finder searches from where your load ends back toward home, and every load card shows net profit after driver pay, fuel, maintenance and deadhead.

It's $49.99 a month after a 7-day free trial, no card needed to start. Cancel anytime.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I book two Amazon Relay loads at the same time?
You book each spot load on its own. Amazon's load board guide doesn't describe booking several in one action. Post A Truck, blocks and contracts reserve more work at once.

### How many hours can my driver drive in a day for back-to-back loads?
Under FMCSA rules, 11 hours of driving within a 14-hour window after 10 consecutive hours off duty. All loads in the day count toward it.

### How far ahead can I post my truck on Amazon Relay?
Up to two weeks ahead with Post A Truck. Amazon doesn't publish a limit on how many posts you can have open.

### How much does cancelling a load hurt my Relay score?
Amazon doesn't publish the amount. It says cancellations count against your acceptance metric, and the closer to pickup, the bigger the penalty.

### Do I need a certain grade to book contracts?
Yes. Amazon says new contracts need a B grade or better, and you can lose booked contracts if you drop below C+.

### Does Amazon post Relay loads on other load boards?
No. Amazon tenders its loads only through Relay. See our [Amazon Relay loads guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-loads/) for what's on the board.
